#!/usr/bin/env bash
# lib.sh — shared helpers for the S5 ops scripts in this folder (bin/).
# Sourced, never executed directly. Shared because every script here needs
# the same three things: loud logging, loud death, and a validated HTTP GET.
#
# Rule for this task folder: an ops evidence script must never silently
# degrade. Every helper below either succeeds completely or reports a clear
# error and returns non-zero, so a baseline built from these scripts is
# trustworthy.

# log <message...> — timestamped progress line on stderr. stdout stays clean
# because the scripts print evidence tables (jsonl/tsv) on stdout.
log() {
  printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >&2
}

# die <message...> — report a clear, fatal setup/usage error and exit 1.
# Used where there is nothing to salvage (missing tool, unreachable API,
# bad arguments). Runtime per-item failures are handled by the callers
# (recorded, counted, non-zero exit at the end) — see fleet-recount.sh.
die() {
  log "FATAL: $*"
  exit 1
}

# require_commands <cmd...> — fail before touching anything if a tool is
# missing, so the failure is about the environment, not about half-written
# evidence files.
require_commands() {
  local missing=() cmd
  for cmd in "$@"; do
    command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$cmd")
  done
  if [ "${#missing[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    die "missing required commands: ${missing[*]} — install them or run on the runner host"
  fi
}

# write_atomic <dest> <src-file> — copy src-file next to dest and rename over
# it, so a crashed run never leaves a half-written evidence file that looks
# complete. Same directory => the final mv is an atomic rename.
# Returns non-zero (and leaves dest untouched) when either step fails.
write_atomic() {
  # NOTE: tmp gets its own statement on purpose. `local dest="$1" ...
  # tmp="$dest.tmp.$$"` in ONE declaration does NOT see the just-assigned
  # dest — bash expands it from the caller's scope, so it only worked while
  # every caller happened to have its own $dest (and died with
  # `dest: unbound variable` otherwise). Separate statements, no surprise.
  local dest="$1" src="$2" tmp
  tmp="$dest.tmp.$$"
  if ! cp "$src" "$tmp"; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: cannot write $dest (copy step failed)"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! mv "$tmp" "$dest"; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: cannot write $dest (rename step failed)"
    return 1
  fi
}

# api_get_json <url> <dest> — GET url into dest as validated JSON.
#   - retries transient network failures (curl --retry-connrefused)
#   - fails on any HTTP error status (curl -f, so a 500/404 body is NOT kept)
#   - refuses to store a 200 body that is not valid JSON (an HTML error page
#     must never end up in the evidence store)
#   - writes dest atomically
# Returns non-zero with a clear stderr line on any failure.
api_get_json() {
  local url="$1" dest="$2" tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if ! curl -sfS -m 60 --retry 3 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 2 -o "$tmp" "$url"; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: GET $url failed (HTTP error or host unreachable after retries)"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! jq -e 'type == "object" or type == "array"' "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: GET $url returned a body that is not valid JSON — refusing to store it in $dest"
    return 1
  fi
  # Propagate the write result explicitly: without this, the status of the
  # `rm` below would mask a failed store and the caller would trust a file
  # that was never written.
  local write_rc=0
  write_atomic "$dest" "$tmp" || write_rc=$?
  rm -f "$tmp"
  return "$write_rc"
}

# validate_label <label> — recount/snapshot labels become file- and directory
# names (recount-<label>.jsonl, raw/<label>/...), so they must be a single
# safe path segment. Without this a label like "../../x" would write evidence
# outside the task folder.
validate_label() {
  local label="$1"
  if ! [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ ]]; then
    die "bad label '$label' — use letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore only, starting with a letter or digit (e.g. before, mid-1431)"
  fi
}

# validate_task_prefix <prefix...> — task ids/prefixes get interpolated into
# shell commands (locally and over ssh) by e5-sweep.sh, so they must be hex
# and dashes only. Accepts a short prefix (8 hex chars) or a full UUID.
# This is the injection guard for the sweep: anything else is rejected before
# any command runs.
validate_task_prefix() {
  local p
  for p in "$@"; do
    if ! [[ "$p" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}(-[0-9a-fA-F]{4,12})*$ ]]; then
      die "bad task id prefix '$p' — expected 8 hex chars plus optional -hex groups (e.g. 7f6220c3 or the full UUID)"
    fi
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — record the fleet matrix
# (GET /runners + GET /deploy/status) and a per-runner convergence verdict.
# READ-ONLY against the backend; safe to run any time, any number of times.
#
# Outputs in <outdir>:
#   runners-<stamp>.json        raw GET /runners payload (evidence)
#   runners-<stamp>.tsv         flat fleet table incl. build sha/builtAt
#   deploy-status-<stamp>.json  raw GET /deploy/status payload
#   verdict-<stamp>.txt         one line per named runner: CONVERGED or the reasons why not
#
# Convergence rule (S5 success criterion 1): runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the
# running build's reported git sha contains the fix commit — verified locally
# with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fixCommit> <buildSha>`, because a version
# string alone cannot prove which code is running. If the runner reports no
# build sha, the verdict says so instead of guessing.
#
# Knobs (env):
#   KAINBAIN_API_BASE            default http://192.168.1.206:3100
#   KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS    default "local-alpha,server2-alpha"
#   KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT       default 046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4 (the 046a6391 deterministic-git-failure change)
#
# Exit codes: 0 snapshot written (converged or not — read verdict-<stamp>.txt);
#   1 setup or API failure (nothing trustworthy written);
#   3 snapshot written, --require-converged given, but not all named runners converged.
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

# fix_in_build <buildSha|""|null> — prints true/false/null. null = cannot tell
# (no sha reported, or sha unknown to the local repo). Uses the local Kainbain
# checkout as the commit database — read-only git queries only.
fix_in_build() {
  local sha="$1" repo_root="$2" fix_commit="$3"
  if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ "$sha" = "null" ]; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if ! git -C "$repo_root" cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if git -C "$repo_root" merge-base --is-ancestor "$fix_commit" "$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo true
  else
    echo false
  fi
}

# verdict_for <runners.json> <runnerId> — prints the verdict JSON object for one
# runner (jq/runner-verdict.jq + the git ancestry check).
verdict_for() {
  local runners_json="$1" runner_id="$2" repo_root="$3" fix_commit="$4"
  local runner sha fix
  runner="$(jq -c --arg id "$runner_id" '.[] | select(.runnerId == $id) // empty' "$runners_json")"
  if [ -z "$runner" ]; then
    printf '{"runnerId":"%s","converged":false,"reasons":["runner not present in GET /runners (offline/revoked?)"]}\n' "$runner_id"
    return 0
  fi
  sha="$(printf '%s' "$runner" | jq -r '.facts.versions.build.sha // ""')"
  fix="$(fix_in_build "$sha" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
  jq -n -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runner-verdict.jq" --argjson runner "$runner" --argjson fixInBuild "$fix"
}

main() {
  require_commands curl jq git date mktemp
  local outdir="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$outdir" ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged]"
  local require_converged=0
  if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
    [ "$2" = "--require-converged" ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — unexpected argument '$2'"
    require_converged=1
  fi
  [ $# -le 2 ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — unexpected extra argument '$3'"

  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
  local named="${KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS:-local-alpha,server2-alpha}"
  [ -n "${named//[[:space:],]/}" ] || die "no named runners to check (KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS is empty) — nothing to do"
  local fix_commit="${KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT:-046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4}"
  local task_dir repo_root stamp
  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
  repo_root="$(git -C "$task_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
  # Second precision: two snapshots in the same minute must not overwrite each other.
  stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
  mkdir -p "$outdir"

  log "runners-snapshot api=$api_base outdir=$outdir named=$named fix=$fix_commit"

  local runners_json="$outdir/runners-$stamp.json" deploy_json="$outdir/deploy-status-$stamp.json"
  api_get_json "$api_base/runners" "$runners_json" \
    || die "GET $api_base/runners failed — nothing written to $outdir"
  # /runners must be an array of runner objects; anything else (an error
  # envelope, an HTML page that slipped through) would make every downstream
  # verdict meaningless, so stop here with a clear message.
  if ! jq -e 'type == "array"' "$runners_json" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -f "$runners_json"
    die "GET $api_base/runners returned valid JSON that is not an array — refusing to build a verdict from it"

    echo "wrote $outdir/runners-$stamp.{json,tsv} $outdir/deploy-status-$stamp.json $outdir/verdict-$stamp.{json,txt}"
  else
    echo "wrote $outdir/runners-$stamp.{json,tsv} $outdir/verdict-$stamp.{json,txt} (no deploy-status: GET /deploy/status failed)"
  fi
  cat "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"
  echo "--- verdict:"
  cat "$verdict_txt"

  if [ "$require_converged" = 1 ] && [ "$all_converged" = 0 ]; then
    log "--require-converged: not all named runners converged (see $verdict_txt)"
    exit 3
  fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# e5-sweep.sh <local|server2> <taskId-prefix>... — GUIDE-05 §4 E5 forensics
# sweep. READ-ONLY: it never reaps, deletes, restarts, updates, or modifies
# anything on either host (survey q9: observe only). For each kb-<taskId>
# it records, per host:
#   - worktrees under the work root: existence + git log + whether a
#     stage-output commit is present in HEAD history
#   - origin branch refs (refs/remotes/origin/kb/<id>* and kb-<id>*): the
#     durable evidence that survives worktree reaping, with git log
#
# Stage-output detection is scoped to the task's OWN branch: a commit counts
# only if its subject matches ^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output. Merged/mirrored
# history regularly contains OTHER tasks' stage-output commits (observed in
# the 2026-11-23 before-sweep: kb/1cae113f commits inside kb/7f6220c3 refs),
# and an unscoped grep would flip the verdict to a false Cause 2/4.
#   - journal lines for the task id (Runner failed / commit / hook / 413 /
#     502 / fetch failed / interrupt)
# and prints one VERDICT line per task:
#   stage-output commit PRESENT  -> Cause 2/4 territory (GUIDE-05 §4)
#   evidence found, commit ABSENT -> Cause 5 suspect (commit/push loop with no landed output)
#   no worktree and no origin ref -> evidence gap (reaped/branch deleted)
#
# Safety: task-id arguments are validated (hex/dashes only — injection guard,
# see lib.sh) and the remote probe is sent base64-encoded, so no argument can
# break out of the remote shell. The probe itself runs only ls/git
# log/for-each-ref/journalctl — all read-only.
#
# Usage:
#   bin/e5-sweep.sh local   7f6220c3 db49d6c6 ...
#   bin/e5-sweep.sh server2 158394ab ...
# Env overrides (used by the test suite, harmless in prod):
#   E5_WORK_ROOT  E5_UNIT  E5_ORIGIN_REPO  E5_JOURNAL_SINCE
# Exit codes: 0 all probed; 1 usage/setup error; 2 some probes failed (output
# still written — the summary says which).
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

# The probe body. Fixed text — the only variables are its five positional
# arguments, all validated or script-controlled before this runs anywhere.
PROBE_SCRIPT='
set -uo pipefail
WORK_ROOT="$1"; UNIT="$2"; ORIGIN_REPO="$3"; PREFIX="$4"; SINCE="$5"
stage_present=0; any_evidence=0

echo "== task kb-$PREFIX"
echo "-- worktrees under $WORK_ROOT:"
found=0
for d in "$WORK_ROOT"/kb-"$PREFIX"*; do
  [ -d "$d" ] || continue
  found=1; any_evidence=1
  echo "   worktree: $d (branch: $(git -C "$d" branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo "?"))"
  git -C "$d" log --format="     %h %ci %s" -5 2>&1 | head -6 || true
  # NB: grep WITHOUT -q on purpose — under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` exits on
  # the first match, git log gets SIGPIPE (rc 141), and the pipeline reports
  # failure even when a match existed. Plain grep reads all input: rc 0 = match.
  if git -C "$d" log --format=%s -20 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output" >/dev/null; then
    stage_present=1
    echo "     stage-output-commit: PRESENT in worktree HEAD history (subject ^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output)"
  else
    echo "     stage-output-commit: absent in worktree HEAD history"
  fi
  for ref in $(git -C "$d" for-each-ref --format="%(refname)" "refs/remotes/origin/kb/$PREFIX"* "refs/remotes/origin/kb-$PREFIX"* 2>/dev/null); do
    echo "   origin ref: $ref"
    git -C "$d" log --format="     %h %ci %s" -5 "$ref" 2>&1 | head -6 || true
    if git -C "$d" log --format=%s -20 "$ref" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output" >/dev/null; then
      stage_present=1
      echo "     stage-output-commit: PRESENT on $ref (subject ^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output)"
    else
      echo "     stage-output-commit: absent on $ref"
    fi
  done
done
[ "$found" = 1 ] || echo "   (no worktree on this host)"

echo "-- origin branch refs in $ORIGIN_REPO (durable, survives worktree reaping):"
if git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  refs=$(git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" for-each-ref --format="%(refname)" "refs/remotes/origin/kb/$PREFIX"* "refs/remotes/origin/kb-$PREFIX"* "refs/heads/kb/$PREFIX"* "refs/heads/kb-$PREFIX"* 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "$refs" ]; then
    any_evidence=1
    while IFS= read -r ref; do
      echo "   $ref"
      git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" log --format="     %h %ci %s" -8 "$ref" 2>&1 | head -9 || true
      if git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" log --format=%s -20 "$ref" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output" >/dev/null; then
        stage_present=1
        echo "     stage-output-commit: PRESENT on $ref (subject ^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output)"
      else
        echo "     stage-output-commit: absent on $ref"
      fi
    done <<EOF
$refs
EOF
  else
    echo "   (no origin branch kb/$PREFIX* or kb-$PREFIX*)"
  fi
else
  echo "   (origin repo $ORIGIN_REPO not available on this host — evidence gap note)"
fi

echo "-- journal ($UNIT, since $SINCE) lines matching $PREFIX:"
if command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  journalctl --user -u "$UNIT" --since "$SINCE" --no-pager 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -i -- "$PREFIX" | grep -iE "Runner failed|commit|hook|413|502|fetch failed|interrupt" | tail -15 | sed "s/^/   /" \
    || echo "   (no matching journal lines)"
else
  echo "   (journalctl not available on this host)"
fi

if [ "$stage_present" = 1 ]; then
  echo "VERDICT kb-$PREFIX: stage-output commit PRESENT -> Cause 2/4 territory (GUIDE-05 §4)"
elif [ "$any_evidence" = 1 ]; then
  echo "VERDICT kb-$PREFIX: evidence found but no stage-output commit -> Cause 5 suspect (commit/push loop, no landed output)"
else
  echo "VERDICT kb-$PREFIX: no worktree and no origin branch -> evidence gap (worktree reaped and branch deleted)"
fi
echo
'

# run_probe <host> <work_root> <unit> <origin_repo> <prefix> <since>
# Local: pipe the probe into bash directly. server2: base64-encode the probe
# and decode it on the remote side, so argument quoting can never inject.
run_probe() {
  local host="$1"; shift
  local args; args="$(printf '%q ' "$@")"
  if [ "$host" = "server2" ]; then
    local b64
    b64="$(printf '%s' "$PROBE_SCRIPT" | base64 -w0)"
    "$SCRIPT_DIR/server2-ssh.sh" "echo $b64 | base64 -d | bash -s -- $args"
  else
    printf '%s' "$PROBE_SCRIPT" | bash -s -- "$@"
  fi
}

main() {
  require_commands bash base64 date git
  local host="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$host" ] || die "usage: e5-sweep.sh <local|server2> <taskId-prefix>..."
  [ "$host" = "local" ] || [ "$host" = "server2" ] || die "host must be 'local' or 'server2', got '$host'"
  shift
  [ $# -ge 1 ] || die "usage: e5-sweep.sh <local|server2> <taskId-prefix>... (at least one task id)"
  validate_task_prefix "$@"

  local task_dir repo_root work_root unit origin_repo since
  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
  repo_root="$(git -C "$task_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
  since="${E5_JOURNAL_SINCE:-2026-11-19}"
  if [ "$host" = "server2" ]; then
    work_root="${E5_WORK_ROOT:-/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work}"
    unit="${E5_UNIT:-kainbain-runner-server2-alpha}"
    origin_repo="${E5_ORIGIN_REPO:-/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/mirrors/Kainbain}"
  else
    work_root="${E5_WORK_ROOT:-$HOME/.kainbain/runner-work}"
    unit="${E5_UNIT:-kainbain-runner-local-alpha}"
    origin_repo="${E5_ORIGIN_REPO:-$repo_root}"
  fi

  echo "## E5 sweep host=$host work_root=$work_root unit=$unit origin_repo=$origin_repo since=$since at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  local failed=0 t
  for t in "$@"; do
    if ! run_probe "$host" "$work_root" "$unit" "$origin_repo" "$t" "$since"; then
      failed=$((failed + 1))
      log "WARN: probe for kb-$t on $host failed — recorded, continuing with the next task"
      echo "VERDICT kb-$t: PROBE FAILED on $host (see stderr) — treat as evidence gap"
      echo
    fi
  done
  echo "## E5 sweep done: $# task(s), $failed probe failure(s) at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
    log "exiting 2: $failed probe(s) failed"
    exit 2
  fi
}

if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
  main "$@"
fi

# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — S5: Roll out 0.2.x runners and run fleet before/after interrupt recount

Task: `683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c` (RESPONSE.md S5 of `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4`).
Type: ops + verification. No code changes, no new unit tests.
Date: 2026-11-23. Status: BEFORE + E5 delivered under the q3-fallback
(see `RUN-LOG.md`, `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md`, `E5-SWEEP.md`, `BASELINE.md`);
the AFTER recount is a scheduled follow-up gated on a human PROD-ACTION
(raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the fix-bearing release).

## Goal

Confirm both production runners (`local-alpha`, `server2-alpha`) converge via the
normal idle-update channel to a build containing the deterministic-git-failure fix
(`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`), then prove with fleet-wide
before/after counts that the 0.2.x rollout resolves the "bare interrupt" class:
bare interrupts drop to ~0, reasons name Causes 1/3/4, and deterministic commit
failures surface as FAILED completions with `gitFailure` payloads instead of
interrupts. Record the post-rollout counts as the new baseline for S1–S4.

## Success criteria

1. `GET /runners` versions recorded before AND after; both named runners observed
   on a `0.2.x` build whose release contains `046a6391` (verified via
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0`, not by version string alone).
2. WIDE_NET §2 counts + GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script re-run on the same scope,
   recorded in the task folder as before/after tables.
3. S5-attributable signals move as predicted: bare interrupts → ~0 on new
   interrupts, `with_reason` names Causes 1/3/4, deterministic commit failures
   appear as FAILED + `gitFailure` (never interrupts). (Cap-escalation and label
   fixes are S1/S6 territory — see §"Attribution boundaries".)
4. E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 §4) executed for every remaining post-`finished`
   interrupt: each classified commit-present (Cause 2/4) or commit-absent
   (Cause 5 suspect), with evidence or an explicit evidence-gap note.
5. Post-rollout baseline recorded in the task folder and usable by S1–S4 as their
   "before" reference (counts + runner versions + backend build + window dates).
6. Zero forced restarts, zero reaped exhibit worktrees, zero agent re-runs:
   observe-only throughout (q9 constraint).

## Grounded facts (verified 2026-11-23 in this checkout)

- HEAD is `7ac148ce` and contains `046a6391` (verified: `git merge-base
  --is-ancestor 046a6391 HEAD` → YES). `046a6391` is the 17-file
  deterministic-git-failure change (daemon branch, `shared/gitFailure/*`).
- `runner/version.json` reads `runnerVersion: 0.2.0`.
  **CORRECTED 2026-11-23 (review F1): tag existence ≠ tag content.**
  `runner-v0.2.0` (`8460e4a8`, 2026-11-19) predates the fix (`046a6391`,
  merged 2026-11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`):
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` → NO, and
  `shared/gitFailure.js` is absent at the tag. A NEW tag `runner-v0.2.1`
  (created 2026-11-23 11:30:02Z from main `65580333`) DOES contain the fix
  (merge-base YES, `shared/gitFailure.js` present, `runnerVersion 0.2.1`).
  Remaining rollout gates: the backend recommended knob (still `0.1.0` at
  12:22Z — runbook step 5, human PROD-ACTION) + per-runner idle converge.
  Never move `runner-v0.2.0`; the fleet converges to `0.2.1` (or newer).
- Recommended-knob wiring: `api/config/schema.js` key `runnerRecommendedVersion`
  (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION`), **default `0.1.0`**. The live value
  must be read at execution time — the default alone cannot confirm the rollout
  is switched on (this is survey q1).
- Runner endpoints exist: `GET /runners` → `runnerRegistry.list()` (fleet
  matrix: versions, badges, update status), `GET /runners/monitor`,
  per-runner `pendingCommands`/`requestUpdate` acks (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`).
- Baseline to beat (WIDE_NET §2, project `0fd41821`, 61 tasks, 2026-11-21):
  118 runner-path interrupts (96 local-alpha / 22 server2-alpha), 49 with
  reason (all cap refusals), 69 bare, 99 ≤15 s after `started` (median 4.7 s),
  15 ≥2 min after `started`, 42 death-streak escalations, 0 server-restart
  interrupts, 100 `Auto-resumed after server restart` rows.
- API base for prod reads: `http://192.168.1.206:3100` (`localhost:3100`
  refuses connections from this runner host, per TICKETS doc).
- E5 exhibits are **already absent on this host**: no `kb-158394ab`,
  `kb-db49d6c6`, `kb-1cae113f`, `kb-7f6220c3` under the server2-alpha work
  root (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_WORK_ROOT=/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work`,
  only 5 unrelated `kb-*` dirs present). The local-alpha host
  (`192.168.1.206`, `~server`) is unchecked — the sweep must check there
  first and treat absence as an evidence gap with fallbacks (§Phase 2).
- GUIDE-05 §4's path `~/.kainbain/kb-$t` is stale for server2-alpha; the real
  layout is `$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_WORK_ROOT/kb-<taskId>*`. Resolve the work root
  per host before sweeping.

Task: `683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c` (RESPONSE.md S5 of `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4`).
Type: ops + verification. No code changes, no new unit tests.
Date: 2026-11-23. Status: BEFORE + E5 delivered under the q3-fallback
(see `RUN-LOG.md`, `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md`, `E5-SWEEP.md`, `BASELINE.md`);
the AFTER recount is a scheduled follow-up gated on a human PROD-ACTION
(raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the fix-bearing release).

## Goal

Confirm both production runners (`local-alpha`, `server2-alpha`) converge via the
normal idle-update channel to a build containing the deterministic-git-failure fix
(`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`), then prove with fleet-wide
before/after counts that the 0.2.x rollout resolves the "bare interrupt" class:
bare interrupts drop to ~0, reasons name Causes 1/3/4, and deterministic commit
failures surface as FAILED completions with `gitFailure` payloads instead of
interrupts. Record the post-rollout counts as the new baseline for S1–S4.

## Success criteria

1. `GET /runners` versions recorded before AND after; both named runners observed
   on a `0.2.x` build whose release contains `046a6391` (verified via
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0`, not by version string alone).
2. WIDE_NET §2 counts + GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script re-run on the same scope,
   recorded in the task folder as before/after tables.
3. S5-attributable signals move as predicted: bare interrupts → ~0 on new
   interrupts, `with_reason` names Causes 1/3/4, deterministic commit failures
   appear as FAILED + `gitFailure` (never interrupts). (Cap-escalation and label
   fixes are S1/S6 territory — see §"Attribution boundaries".)
4. E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 §4) executed for every remaining post-`finished`
   interrupt: each classified commit-present (Cause 2/4) or commit-absent
   (Cause 5 suspect), with evidence or an explicit evidence-gap note.
5. Post-rollout baseline recorded in the task folder and usable by S1–S4 as their
   "before" reference (counts + runner versions + backend build + window dates).
6. Zero forced restarts, zero reaped exhibit worktrees, zero agent re-runs:
   observe-only throughout (q9 constraint).

## Approach — make observation easy, then observe

This task changes nothing; its failure mode is fuzzy, non-reproducible numbers.
So Phase 0 ("make change easy") builds all reusable observation tooling first —
frozen scripts, record templates, access checks, and the BEFORE snapshot — and
only then do the time-ordered phases run. Big/volatile evidence comes early:
the BEFORE recount and the E5 sweep run before the convergence wait, because
interrupts keep accruing and worktree exhibits keep getting reaped (all four
E5 seed exhibits are already absent from this host). The long pole — idle
convergence at most daily per runner — waits in Phase 3 without blocking
Phase 1/2 evidence.

Attribution boundaries (what S5 may and may not claim): S1 (cap counting),
S2-backend (413 limit), S4 (transient tolerance), S6 (labels/counts) all change
the same signals. S5's after-recount MUST record the backend build number
(`GET /deploy/status`) and which sibling fixes have landed, and split new
interrupts by timestamp against each runner's converge time. Only interrupts
timestamped after a runner converged to 0.2.x count as "after" for S5.
`escalated` dropping is an S1 signal, not an S5 gate; the S5 gates are bare→~0,
reasons present, and FAILED+`gitFailure` instead of commit-loop interrupts.

## Phase 2 — E5 forensics sweep (early: exhibits are volatile)

For each post-`finished` interrupt from 1.2 (seeds: `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`,
`1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`, plus any new ones from 1.1):

2.1 Worktree check per host (read-only, never reap): resolve the runner work
    root on that host first, then
    `git -C $WORK_ROOT/kb-<taskId>* log --oneline -3` and look for a
    stage-output commit matching the execution window. Present → Cause 2/4
    territory; absent → Cause 5 suspect. Record exact SHAs or exact absence.
2.2 Journal join (same host, same window): `Runner failed:` line text +
    restart-counter deltas — names hook/commit vs 413 vs 502/fetch-fail.
2.3 Fallback chain when a worktree is absent (already the case on server2-alpha
    for all four seeds): (a) check the sibling host; (b) check `origin` for the
    stage-output SHA (pushed = commit succeeded, Cause 2/4); (c) journal line
    alone; (d) if all absent, record an explicit evidence gap — never guess.
2.4 Verdict per interrupt: Cause-2/4 vs Cause-5-covered-by-`046a6391` vs
    Cause-5-NOT-covered. The third verdict is the ONLY trigger for new code:
    if and only if E5 finds commit-loop cases `046a6391` does not cover
    (a deterministic failure class outside `HOOK_REJECTED`/`COMMIT_FAILED`/
    `MERGE_CONFLICT` that still crash-loops on 0.2.x), file a NEW Cause-5
    code ticket with the journal line + worktree state + failing class.

Gate: `E5-SWEEP.md` with one row per post-`finished` interrupt (evidence or
gap) + the ticket/no-ticket decision with reasoning.

## Phase 3 — Convergence watch (the long pole; observe only)

3.1 Poll `GET /runners` on a slow cadence (30–60 min) and snapshot each poll.
    Per runner record: running version + build facts, `updateAvailable` /
    `belowMinimum` / `updateStatus` badges, pending vs acked `requestUpdate`
    (nudge cooldown is 24 h), busy/idle, pinned-vs-Latest.
3.2 Declare a runner converged at the first poll showing a 0.2.x build whose
    release contains `046a6391`; record the converge timestamp per runner in
    `RUN-LOG.md`. Both converged → proceed to Phase 4 (q3 default).
3.3 If a runner stalls (badge never clears past 24–48 h): triage READ-ONLY per
    the runbook ("a runner says out of date") — `entrypoint: direct` vs
    wrapper, `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` opt-out, pinned version, pin
    older than running, recommended knob above every release, `updateStatus`
    failure reason — and record the blocking cause. Fixes (migrate, flip the
    switch, Update button) are PROD-ACTION: propose, do not perform.
3.4 NEVER to speed convergence: force-restart mid-assignment, Update-on-busy,
    reaping worktrees, re-running parked tasks. Any of these manufactures the
    interrupts being measured (q9 / PROD-ACTION ban).

Gate: per-runner converge timestamps, or a stalled-runner triage note with a
named blocking cause. Under the q3-fallback (before-now/stop), Phase 3 becomes
a scheduled follow-up run instead of a same-run wait.

## Validation & assurance plan (how we know it worked)

No unit tests by design (ops task — RESPONSE.md S5: "No new unit tests;
deliverable is the recount + version record"). Assurance instead comes from
executed procedures with saved evidence, each claim cross-checked two ways:

| Claim | Primary evidence | Independent cross-check |
|---|---|---|
| Runners on fix build | `GET /runners` version facts | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` + heartbeat build fields |
| Bare → ~0 | Fleet script `bare` count post-converge | Reason-vocabulary audit (1.3): every new interrupt carries a reason naming a cause |
| No commit crash-loops | FAILED + `gitFailure` completions, no interrupt row | Journal: single `commit failed` per incident, no restart storm |
| E5 classification | Worktree stage-output-commit presence | Journal `Runner failed:` line + origin SHA check |
| No server-restart orphans | `server_restart` count stays 0 | Backend build/`engine.updatedAt` divergence log (Cause-6 upkeep) |

Per-phase gates above double as the test plan: a phase is done only when its
artifact file exists with the named content. Negative controls: (a) BEFORE
snapshot must show still-bare new interrupts (proves the premise that 0.1.0
emits no reasons); (b) any reasoned non-cap interrupt pre-converge, or any
bare interrupt post-converge, fails its gate and must be explained, not
averaged away. Docs assurance: every record file carries timestamps, raw
command output (or the raw JSON), and the exact re-run command.

timestamped after a runner converged to 0.2.x count as "after" for S5.

reasons present, and FAILED+`gitFailure` instead of commit-loop interrupts.

## Phase 0 — Setup: tooling, access, knob state, BEFORE snapshot (first)

    effective decision per question at the top of the run log.
0.2 Access checks (read-only, stop on first refusal and record it):
    `GET /status/observability`, `GET /tasks?projectId=0fd41821` (expect ~61+
    tasks — confirms project id scope for q4), `GET /runners`,
    `GET /deploy/status` (backend build number), journal read on both hosts,
    work-root listing on both hosts.
0.3 Knob state (q1): record live `runnerRecommendedVersion` /
    `runnerMinVersion` (backend config endpoint or operator-read env).
    Under the default assumption do NOT change them; under the q1-fallback,
    raise recommended to `0.2.0` (config only, no restart) and record old→new.
0.4 Freeze the observation kit in this task folder so S1–S4 re-run identically:
    - `bin/fleet-recount.sh` — GUIDE-07 §5 script pinned to the API base +
      project id, plus a `jq -s` aggregation pass emitting the WIDE_NET §2
      table rows (runner_interrupts, with_reason, bare, ≤15 s, ≥2 min,
      auto_resumed, server_restart, escalated, per-runner split).
    - `bin/runners-snapshot.sh` — `GET /runners` raw JSON → timestamped file.

    fleet script → `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md` (per-task rows + §2 table). This is the
    "before" half of the rollout proof; everything after compares to it.
0.6 Verify release content: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0`
    (must print YES — proves the 0.2.0 release actually carries the fix).

state recorded. All later phases are mechanical re-runs of Phase 0 tooling.

## Phase 1 — BEFORE recount analysis (same data as 0.5, second lens)

1.1 Recompute the WIDE_NET §2 table from the BEFORE snapshot and diff it against
    the 11-21 baseline (new interrupts since 11-21 are expected — runners are
    still 0.1.0; every new one should still be bare, which itself re-confirms
    the "until it lands" premise).
1.2 List every post-`finished` interrupt (≥2 min after `started`, or explicit
    `finished`→interrupt pair) with task id + timestamps — this is the E5
    worklist for Phase 2.
1.3 Confirm the reason vocabulary on new interrupts: cap refusals still reasoned,
    everything else bare. Any *reasoned non-cap* interrupt before convergence
    would contradict the "0.1.0 emits no reasons" premise — flag, don't ignore.

Gate: `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md` holds §2 table + diff vs 11-21 + E5 worklist.

## Phase 2 — E5 forensics sweep (early: exhibits are volatile)

`1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`, plus any new ones from 1.1):

2.1 Worktree check per host (read-only, never reap): resolve the runner work
    root on that host first, then
    `git -C $WORK_ROOT/kb-<taskId>* log --oneline -3` and look for a
    stage-output commit matching the execution window. Present → Cause 2/4
    territory; absent → Cause 5 suspect. Record exact SHAs or exact absence.
2.2 Journal join (same host, same window): `Runner failed:` line text +
    restart-counter deltas — names hook/commit vs 413 vs 502/fetch-fail.
2.3 Fallback chain when a worktree is absent (already the case on server2-alpha
    for all four seeds): (a) check the sibling host; (b) check `origin` for the
    stage-output SHA (pushed = commit succeeded, Cause 2/4); (c) journal line
    alone; (d) if all absent, record an explicit evidence gap — never guess.
2.4 Verdict per interrupt: Cause-2/4 vs Cause-5-covered-by-`046a6391` vs
    Cause-5-NOT-covered. The third verdict is the ONLY trigger for new code:
    if and only if E5 finds commit-loop cases `046a6391` does not cover
    (a deterministic failure class outside `HOOK_REJECTED`/`COMMIT_FAILED`/
    `MERGE_CONFLICT` that still crash-loops on 0.2.x), file a NEW Cause-5
    code ticket with the journal line + worktree state + failing class.

Gate: `E5-SWEEP.md` with one row per post-`finished` interrupt (evidence or
gap) + the ticket/no-ticket decision with reasoning.

## Phase 3 — Convergence watch (the long pole; observe only)

3.1 Poll `GET /runners` on a slow cadence (30–60 min) and snapshot each poll.
    Per runner record: running version + build facts, `updateAvailable` /
    `belowMinimum` / `updateStatus` badges, pending vs acked `requestUpdate`
    (nudge cooldown is 24 h), busy/idle, pinned-vs-Latest.
3.2 Declare a runner converged at the first poll showing a 0.2.x build whose
    release contains `046a6391`; record the converge timestamp per runner in
    `RUN-LOG.md`. Both converged → proceed to Phase 4 (q3 default).
3.3 If a runner stalls (badge never clears past 24–48 h): triage READ-ONLY per
    the runbook ("a runner says out of date") — `entrypoint: direct` vs
    wrapper, `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` opt-out, pinned version, pin
    older than running, recommended knob above every release, `updateStatus`
    failure reason — and record the blocking cause. Fixes (migrate, flip the
    switch, Update button) are PROD-ACTION: propose, do not perform.
3.4 NEVER to speed convergence: force-restart mid-assignment, Update-on-busy,
    reaping worktrees, re-running parked tasks. Any of these manufactures the
    interrupts being measured (q9 / PROD-ACTION ban).

named blocking cause. Under the q3-fallback (before-now/stop), Phase 3 becomes
a scheduled follow-up run instead of a same-run wait.

    hook/commit lines (expect single `commit failed (...)` + FAILED, no

    have deployed, and any deploys that restarted the backend in-window

Gate: `RECOUNT-AFTER.md` with the post-converge-gated verdict per S5 gate
(pass/fail + counts), plus the confound ledger.

5.1 Write `BASELINE.md`: the new S1–S4 reference — BEFORE/AFTER §2 tables,
    per-runner versions + converge timestamps, backend builds, window dates,
    E5 verdicts, open evidence gaps, and the exact re-run commands (Phase 0 kit).

    never waited); S1/S6 confirm against `BASELINE.md` + their own deploys.

    that no new Cause-5 code is needed.
5.3 Review-checklist pass (RESPONSE.md): no PROD command ran without permission;
    exhibit worktrees untouched; recount recorded before any victory claim.

Gate: `BASELINE.md` present and self-contained — a stranger can re-run the
whole proof from the kit + this file alone.

## Validation & assurance plan (how we know it worked)

No unit tests by design (ops task — RESPONSE.md S5: "No new unit tests;
deliverable is the recount + version record"). Assurance instead comes from
executed procedures with saved evidence, each claim cross-checked two ways:

| Claim | Primary evidence | Independent cross-check |
|---|---|---|

1|# Runner update runbook
2|
3|Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
4|`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
5|rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
6|that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
7|serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.
8|
9|## Cutting a runner release (normal path)
10|
11|The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.
12|
13|1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
14|   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
15|   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
16|2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
17|   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
18|   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
19|   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
20|3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
21|4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
22|   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
23|   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
24|   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
25|   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
26|   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
27|5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
28|   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
29|   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
30|   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
31|   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
32|   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).
33|
34|## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)
35|
36|When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
37|hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:
38|
39|```
40|git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
41|git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
42|```
43|
44|Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
45|version forward instead.
46|
47|## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)
48|
49|1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
50|   resolves to the prior tag.
51|2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
52|   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
53|   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
54|3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
55|   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
56|   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
57|   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
58|4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
59|   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
60|   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
61|   is cut.
62|
63|Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
64|fleet converged.
65|
66|## Migrating a host to the wrapper
67|
68|Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
69|restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
70|versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
71|the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
72|so the fleet version does not change).
73|
74|Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:
75|
76|```
77|# 1. Pre-check (read-only, safe any time):
78|KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
79|  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service
80|
81|# 2. Rehearse:
82|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id> --dry-run
83|
84|# 3. Migrate (snapshots unit + env, reloads, restarts, re-verifies):
85|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id>
86|```
87|
88|The script refuses to overwrite an existing `current` link and prints
89|revert commands (copy the `.bak-<timestamp>` files back, reload,
90|restart). New installs need no migration: both installers
91|(`scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `startRunner.sh`) already write
92|wrapper-based units. Verify after: `doctor` reports `status: ok` with
93|`entrypoint: wrapper`, and the next heartbeat shows the same version
94|as before.
95|
96|## Restart vs Update (Settings › Runners)
97|
98|Two separate actions, never combined:
99|
100|- **Restart** reboots the runner on its **current version** — no update
101|  check runs. It is destructive: any work running on that runner is
102|  stopped at once (the claim lease expires so the work re-queues, like a
103|  crash). The confirm window names the runner and warns about running
104|  work; use it when a runner looks stuck, not to change versions.
105|  Mechanism: the daemon writes a `restart-requested` sentinel beside the
106|  install root and exits 0; the wrapper consumes it and boots the SAME
107|  tree again. Restart therefore needs the wrapper entrypoint — a runner
108|  started as bare `node main.js` exits without rebooting (migrate to the
109|  wrapper, above).
110|- **Update** reinstalls the runner onto its **target version** — the
111|  exact pin when the runner is pinned, otherwise the newest compatible
112|  release — and applies only when the runner is idle (never interrupts
113|  work). A busy runner queues the update for the next idle point.
114|
115|## Per-runner version setting
116|
117|Each runner is set to **Latest** (default) or one exact release, via
118|the version dropdown on its Settings › Runners detail panel:
119|
120|- **Latest** tracks the newest release. It auto-updates at the next
121|  idle point (including right after a restart, once idle), and the
122|  backend nudges trailing runners at most daily. A red banner appears
123|  whenever a newer version exists than the one running — update (or
124|  wait for idle) to converge it.
125|- **Pinned** stays on exactly that release. Pinned runners never
126|  auto-update (no nudges, no idle installs, no restart-time installs);
127|  only the manual **Update** button installs the pin, and only when the
128|  pin is newer than the running version — the channel never downgrades,
129|  so a pin older than running shows a softer warning and the Update
130|  button stays disabled with the reason. Pick Latest or a newer pin to
131|  move forward.
132|
133|The dropdown lists Latest plus every fleet-known release (newest
134|first): each runner's running version plus the fleet recommended and
135|minimum knobs — offline-safe, no release catalogue fetch.
136|
137|## Triage: a runner says out of date
138|
139|Start on the runner host (or ask the host owner to run it) — the
140|doctor is read-only and never writes:
141|
142|```
143|$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service
144|```
145|
146|Match the Settings › Runners badge to a cause:
147|
148|- **"update available" that never clears.** The runner trails
149|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (Latest runners) or its pin.
150|  If the doctor says `entrypoint: direct`, migrate to the wrapper
151|  (above) — staged updates can never boot there. If the env shows
152|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` (or `(unset)` with a host-level
153|  opt-out), the runner acked the nudge with "skipped: auto-update is
154|  disabled" — flip that switch. If the runner is pinned, only the
155|  manual Update button installs (pins never auto-update); a pin older
156|  than running refuses with "never downgrades" — pick Latest or a
157|  newer pin. If the recommended knob sits above every published
158|  release, lower it to the newest release. Otherwise the runner is
159|  likely just busy: it converges at the next idle check, or press
160|  Update now (idle-only, never interrupts work). Restart does NOT
161|  clear this — Restart reboots the same version.
162|- **"restart queued" that never clears / restart loop.** The runner
163|  collects `requestRestart` on every heartbeat but never reboots:
164|  check the journal for the `Runner restarting` line. If the line is
165|  there but no reboot follows, the runner is not supervised by the
166|  wrapper (bare `node main.js` exits instead of rebooting — migrate to
167|  the wrapper, above) or the install root is unwritable (look for
168|  `sentinel not written`). A `restart-requested` file left behind by a
169|  crash causes at most one extra boot on the next clean exit — the
170|  wrapper consumes it, never loops. Old runners that predate the
171|  command show a disabled Restart with "too old" guidance instead —
172|  update them manually.
173|- **"below minimum" / 409 loop.** The runner is under
174|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and dispatch refuses it. It
175|  self-updates immediately when idle (interval bypassed). If it
176|  spins, check the journal for `Runner update` lines and treat the
177|  reason like an "update failed" below.
178|- **"update failed".** The next heartbeat carries `updateStatus`
179|  (`state: failed`, `reason`, `at`) — the badge tooltip shows it.
180|  Map the reason prefix: signature/key failure (release not signed
181|  by the pinned key — never hand-edit
182|  `PINNED_RELEASE_PUBLIC_KEY` in `runner/updates/verify.js` for a
183|  cut release); sha mismatch (re-download on next check); no asset
184|  for this platform (release is missing this host's tarball);
185|  incompatible with this backend (no newer release admits this
186|  backend's API — expected while the backend lags the release
187|  line); update lock held (a previous updater is still running or
188|  crashed mid-apply — stale locks self-heal); opted out (see
189|  above). Any failure keeps the old version running; fix the cause
190|  and the next idle check retries.
191|- **"rolled back" in the doctor.** Three crashed boots flipped
192|  `current` back to `previous`. Do not retry blindly: read the
193|  journal for the crash, fix forward with a patch release, and run
194|  the rollback drill above if the release is bad fleet-wide.
195|
196|Backend-side checks: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and
197|`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` values, the fleet matrix row
198|for the runner (`runnerVersion`, `updateAvailable`, `belowMinimum`,
199|`updateStatus`), and whether a `requestUpdate` command is pending or
200|was acked within the last 24h (the auto-nudge cooldown).

59|   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
60|   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
61|   is cut.

64|fleet converged.

69|restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
70|versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
71|the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
72|so the fleet version does not change).

82|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id> --dry-run

85|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id>

92|wrapper-based units. Verify after: `doctor` reports `status: ok` with
93|`entrypoint: wrapper`, and the next heartbeat shows the same version
94|as before.

100|- **Restart** reboots the runner on its **current version** — no update
101|  check runs. It is destructive: any work running on that runner is
102|  stopped at once (the claim lease expires so the work re-queues, like a
103|  crash). The confirm window names the runner and warns about running
104|  work; use it when a runner looks stuck, not to change versions.

163|  collects `requestRestart` on every heartbeat but never reboots:
164|  check the journal for the `Runner restarting` line. If the line is
165|  there but no reboot follows, the runner is not supervised by the

190|  and the next idle check retries.

--- CHANGELOG
# Changelog

All notable changes to KainBain are recorded here in **curated** form. The
per-commit baked history that backs the in-app **Changelog** dialog is generated
by `scripts/generate-changelog.mjs` and served through `GET /deploy/changelog`
(`frontend/src/components/layout/ChangelogModal.jsx`); it remains the exhaustive
source of truth. This file intentionally lists only high-impact changes.

## Update discipline

- Entries are curated **only at release time**, from the `Unreleased` section
  below, when a version tag/deploy is cut. Ordinary PRs are not required to touch
  this file (WP-10, task `8e61e197-cf8a-475e-b330-8cd7fa5a7e30`).
- Keep entries to one line each, grouped under `Added` / `Changed` / `Fixed` /
  `Removed` / `Security`. Reference the PR or task id in parentheses when
  helpful. Do not copy auto-generated commit subjects verbatim.
- After a release, rename the `## [Unreleased]` content to `## [x.y.z] -
  YYYY-MM-DD`.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Separate docs repo per project (stealth mode): a project can keep ALL KainBain information (task docs, plans, reports, and the `.kainbain/` state incl. `project.json`) in a private git repo instead of the main repo, which then stays completely free of KainBain traces. Offered under an Advanced disclosure on project create/import and in Project Settings → Files & Repositories; stored redacted, one docs repo per project (409 on re-claim); runners check the docs repo out adjacent to the main repo with synced `kb/<taskId>` branches and push docs first at stage handoff (task 7f6220c3).

- System Settings gains an About tab (also at `#/system-settings/about`) showing the running UI, backend, and screen-to-server API versions with per-row update guides, a warning banner when a newer release is advertised, and the latest security report summary with a full-report link — all served by the new `GET /status/versions` endpoint. The API row ties the UI-reported contract (`frontend/version.json`) to the backend contract (`api/version.json`) with a compatibility verdict (the same API major stays compatible across asymmetric redeploys, with an alert on mismatch); unadvertised latest-release knobs (`KAINBAIN_LATEST_*_VERSION`) report Up to date, while a missing security report file (`KAINBAIN_SECURITY_REPORT_PATH`) still shows the honest "no security report recorded" state (task c5c465c4).

- Task goals render ` ```mermaid ` fences as inline SVG diagrams in the markdown viewer (mermaid lazy-loads only when a diagram is present and sanitizes at `strict` security level; a broken or unrenderable diagram degrades to its readable source block, never a blank hole), and the `creating-new-tickets` skill now drafts each ticket as its own markdown file under the task directory's `drafts/` folder before POSTing the file's exact contents, so API-created tickets land as structured documents (headings, steps, code, diagrams, image refs) instead of paragraphs; the first-line title, `blockedBy` validation, idempotency, and dedupe behave exactly as before (task 5a38ad45).

- Stage+config attestation for compliance proof: every per-stage wrap-up commit and its stage-history entry now carry the same task+stage config hash (git trailers plus a durable prose token with the commit SHA), verifiable offline with `node scripts/verify-stage-attestation.mjs --repo <path> --task <id>` (see the Stage Attestation site-docs article); clean-tree stages attest with an explicit null commit, and entries predating the feature stay valid without hashes (task d20f0c83).

- API key system for agents and external services (off by default, separate `KAINBAIN_API_KEYS_ENABLED` switch): admin-managed keys with catalogue roles plus narrowing scopes, secret shown once and stored hashed, task mutations gated per key grant, every key action flagged by key name in task history and the audit log, and a per-key usage view — browser sessions and Runners work unchanged with the switch on or off (task ac988ba8).
- Docs article `h2` sections collapse and expand via their headers (chevron toggle, keyboard-operable, Expand all / Collapse all above the article), and headers render larger and bolder for scanning (task e3369ccb).
- Task detail pages and `GET /tasks/:id` now show where a task works (branch, workspace-isolation mode, worktree path) via the additive `workingLocation` field, and a new `Develop Alongside KainBain` site-docs article teaches the pause-edit-resume, separate-branch, and review-gate flows; dirty-tree guard errors now name the blocking paths plus the safe next step for hand edits (task 8dafdce1).
- Per-stage Runner allow/block list at the bottom of stage settings (`Off` / `Only these runners` / `All except these runners`): dispatch, direct claims, and merge leases refuse ineligible Runners loudly while unrestricted stages behave exactly as before (task a3753643).
- Runner model auto-detect for every supported harness (pi, muse, antigravity, vibe, plus honest-empty opencode/codex legs) with per-harness counts and the first leg warning in Settings › Runners next to Re-detect, driven by the existing refresh command (task 2cbe91b6).
- Runner harness auto-detect now probes beyond PATH — standard install dirs (`~/.local/bin`, `~/bin`), each harness's own install dir, `KAINBAIN_*_BIN` overrides, and pi via its `~/.pi/agent` `models.json` snapshot — matching the backend's `discoverHarnesses`, so hosts with an SDK-only pi install (e.g. server2, whose service PATH lacks `~/.pi/agent/bin`) now detect pi and advertise its models in the fleet picker (task 2cbe91b6).
- Runner model discovery fails loud instead of reporting silent zeros: empty pi/muse scans record classified `PI_MODELS_EMPTY` / `MUSE_MSP_*` reasons with fixes in Settings, and re-detection names detected-but-unconfigured harnesses (`harness auto-detect also sees: …`) so a stale harness pin can no longer hide models; new installs record `auto` so every boot re-detects (task 2cbe91b6).
- Per-pipeline base branch: each named workflow can treat a feature branch as its main branch (pipeline settings `Base branch` field, blank = repo default) — new task branches fork off it, the merge stage merges back into it (and pushes it), CI `primary` mode runs on it, and review diffs compare against it; the base is pinned per task at creation so re-pointing a pipeline never retargets in-flight work, and a missing base is auto-created from the repo default tip (task cf4b6847).

### Changed

- Central queue across all pipelines/projects: both dispatch paths (embedded scheduler and runner fleet) and the queue display now sort through one shared seam in `oldest-first` mode by default — the oldest waiting task runs next wherever it lives, with furthest-along as a percentage of its own pipeline as tiebreak — so waiting work on a pipeline you are not viewing no longer starves behind late-stage work on the focused one; the follow-on pass can no longer pre-empt work waiting past the starvation ceiling (built-in 15 min, `KAINBAIN_DISPATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS`), `GET /tasks/queue` without `?projectId=` returns the all-projects queue instead of the UI-focused project, and the queue popup shows per-project waiting counts plus the current worker. Rollback: `KAINBAIN_CENTRAL_QUEUE_ORDER=furthest-along` (task 16d6fbd6).
- Task surfaces read easier: card titles render larger and semibold with the status as a chip (colour dot plus text label), details-tab banner text steps up to body size, and long audit logs preview behind a Show all disclosure (task e3369ccb).
- Runner model precedence stays pin-wins by default (pinned installs skip discovery and advertise exactly their pin across updates); `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1` opts in to survey-q4 discovery-wins, where a non-empty auto-detect result replaces the pin (task 2cbe91b6).
- Consolidated root-level markdown files into `docs/`: moved `CI_SCRIPTS.md`, `PORTABLE_DEPLOYMENT.md`, `agent-docs/`, and `research/phase0-branch-dry-run.md`; deleted 13 obsolete one-off summaries and superseded phase-2 plans (task fc3acfff).
- Merged the ALL / FAILED / HUMAN ONLY board pills into the unified search bar as `!` system filters (e.g. `auth #Dev !failed`): same dropdown, chips, and Any/All toggle as `#` tags; unknown `!tokens` stay as text; future native filters register via `frontend/src/components/workflow/systemFilters/` (task c213d3a9).

### Fixed

- Runners pick up waiting work on every pipeline, not just the viewed one: dispatch and direct claims now resolve each task's stage from its own pipeline instead of the active pipeline's stages, so a task on a non-active pipeline is matched against its own harness/model/tier/stage instead of being excluded or mis-served; tasks pointing at deleted stages park instead of running as another stage's job, and the pipeline switcher/toast now say "viewing" so the viewed pipeline no longer reads as the only live one (task 55460086).
- Stale Runner pins no longer pose as available models: the central model catalogue confirms every harness-scoped id against the claimant's own successful scans and marks contradicted ids unavailable with the stale-pin reason and claimant list (still shown in their section, never hidden); inconclusive signals (failed scans, old Runners, legacy/bare ids) keep trusting the advertisement, and dispatch refuses contradicted pins like unoffered models instead of routing work where the harness menu proved them absent — while the operator's `availableModels` override keeps its explicit say everywhere (task 9d2b75a2).
- Newly released harness models are selectable automatically: pinned Runners (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS`/`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL`) now still run model auto-discovery and advertise pin ∪ discovered ids (`modelSource: "pinned+discovered"`), so a brand-new model (e.g. a fresh Muse release) reaches the central model catalogue and every picker without editing the pin — the pin itself is never dropped; the muse discovery probe also passes `--provider` like the backend MSP catalogue so both read the host identically (task 9d2b75a2).
- Runner fleet cards stay named on every pipeline page: `GET /runners/monitor` now carries each assignment's own project/task/stage identity, the widget renders it even when the viewer looks at another pipeline, and "Open task" jumps to the job in its pipeline (task 350ca162).
- Bottom-bar queue number counts only tasks waiting to be picked up (never running, blocked, paused, failed, cancelled, or waiting-human tasks), and the queue popup lists exactly that same set in dispatch order (task 6d3c9317).
- Survey answers survive later Runner stages: Runner task-file shipments merge into the backend survey (new rounds land, saved answers are kept) instead of overwriting them with stale worktree copies; the question-me prompt also names the exact backend-resolved file for alias/extension-less configs (task fbcaef1d).
- Bottom (now-playing) bar on mobile is horizontally scrollable, so all runners are reachable instead of only the first (task a654a254).
- Pipeline releases published from the deploy tip worktree are synced back to the primary `dist/` and verified there; a stranded release now fails Publish loudly, and the Update stage verifies the installed commit against the last-publish pointer instead of reporting "already current" (task a654a254).
- Bottom (now-playing) bar stays live with no page refresh: runner boxes follow stage/task changes within one 5s fleet poll (all fleet surfaces share a single poller), and the queue chip refreshes within about a second of task activity with a 15s safety poll; background tabs pause polling and catch up on return (task ed00c209).
- Remote runners now self-update reliably: version selection is compatibility-gated (newest release whose manifest `requires.backendApi` admits the backend, never past it), the backend advertises its update directive and auto-nudges outdated command-capable runners daily, releases are cut by the publish pipeline instead of manual tags, and systemd installs boot through the self-update wrapper (with a migration script plus a read-only `doctor` for triage); see `docs/runner-update-runbook.md` (task 82e49a05).
- Stage prompts no longer name phantom reports: `# Previous Reports` (and `{{previousReports}}` / `{{latestReport*}}`) enumerate the files actually present in `docs/tasks/<taskId>/` — newest first, capped at `KAINBAIN_TASK_REPORTS_MAX_PROMPT_REFS` (default 5) with an overflow pointer, plus an explicit none-yet line for empty folders — so history entries whose file is gone are omitted instead of presented as available; report metadata keeps those entries flagged `missingOnDisk` for API/UI consumers (task 4f927ecb).
- Runner commit/hook failures are now visible and actionable: a refused commit (e.g. the pre-commit binary guard rejecting corrupt PNGs) reports as a failed completion with structured detail instead of dying in the runner journal, the task shows a "Commit Failed" callout (hook, command, affected files, remedy, full output) replacing the stale error, and the runner stays alive instead of crash-looping; after three consecutive same-signature failures the task parks (auto-dispatch and direct claims skip it) until an operator retries, resumes, or moves it (task 1cae113f).

--- CHANGELOG
# Changelog

All notable changes to KainBain are recorded here in **curated** form. The
per-commit baked history that backs the in-app **Changelog** dialog is generated
by `scripts/generate-changelog.mjs` and served through `GET /deploy/changelog`
(`frontend/src/components/layout/ChangelogModal.jsx`); it remains the exhaustive
source of truth. This file intentionally lists only high-impact changes.

## Update discipline

- Entries are curated **only at release time**, from the `Unreleased` section
  below, when a version tag/deploy is cut. Ordinary PRs are not required to touch
  this file (WP-10, task `8e61e197-cf8a-475e-b330-8cd7fa5a7e30`).
- Keep entries to one line each, grouped under `Added` / `Changed` / `Fixed` /
  `Removed` / `Security`. Reference the PR or task id in parentheses when
  helpful. Do not copy auto-generated commit subjects verbatim.
- After a release, rename the `## [Unreleased]` content to `## [x.y.z] -
  YYYY-MM-DD`.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Separate docs repo per project (stealth mode): a project can keep ALL KainBain information (task docs, plans, reports, and the `.kainbain/` state incl. `project.json`) in a private git repo instead of the main repo, which then stays completely free of KainBain traces. Offered under an Advanced disclosure on project create/import and in Project Settings → Files & Repositories; stored redacted, one docs repo per project (409 on re-claim); runners check the docs repo out adjacent to the main repo with synced `kb/<taskId>` branches and push docs first at stage handoff (task 7f6220c3).

- System Settings gains an About tab (also at `#/system-settings/about`) showing the running UI, backend, and screen-to-server API versions with per-row update guides, a warning banner when a newer release is advertised, and the latest security report summary with a full-report link — all served by the new `GET /status/versions` endpoint. The API row ties the UI-reported contract (`frontend/version.json`) to the backend contract (`api/version.json`) with a compatibility verdict (the same API major stays compatible across asymmetric redeploys, with an alert on mismatch); unadvertised latest-release knobs (`KAINBAIN_LATEST_*_VERSION`) report Up to date, while a missing security report file (`KAINBAIN_SECURITY_REPORT_PATH`) still shows the honest "no security report recorded" state (task c5c465c4).

- Task goals render ` ```mermaid ` fences as inline SVG diagrams in the markdown viewer (mermaid lazy-loads only when a diagram is present and sanitizes at `strict` security level; a broken or unrenderable diagram degrades to its readable source block, never a blank hole), and the `creating-new-tickets` skill now drafts each ticket as its own markdown file under the task directory's `drafts/` folder before POSTing the file's exact contents, so API-created tickets land as structured documents (headings, steps, code, diagrams, image refs) instead of paragraphs; the first-line title, `blockedBy` validation, idempotency, and dedupe behave exactly as before (task 5a38ad45).

- Stage+config attestation for compliance proof: every per-stage wrap-up commit and its stage-history entry now carry the same task+stage config hash (git trailers plus a durable prose token with the commit SHA), verifiable offline with `node scripts/verify-stage-attestation.mjs --repo <path> --task <id>` (see the Stage Attestation site-docs article); clean-tree stages attest with an explicit null commit, and entries predating the feature stay valid without hashes (task d20f0c83).

- API key system for agents and external services (off by default, separate `KAINBAIN_API_KEYS_ENABLED` switch): admin-managed keys with catalogue roles plus narrowing scopes, secret shown once and stored hashed, task mutations gated per key grant, every key action flagged by key name in task history and the audit log, and a per-key usage view — browser sessions and Runners work unchanged with the switch on or off (task ac988ba8).
- Docs article `h2` sections collapse and expand via their headers (chevron toggle, keyboard-operable, Expand all / Collapse all above the article), and headers render larger and bolder for scanning (task e3369ccb).
- Task detail pages and `GET /tasks/:id` now show where a task works (branch, workspace-isolation mode, worktree path) via the additive `workingLocation` field, and a new `Develop Alongside KainBain` site-docs article teaches the pause-edit-resume, separate-branch, and review-gate flows; dirty-tree guard errors now name the blocking paths plus the safe next step for hand edits (task 8dafdce1).
- Per-stage Runner allow/block list at the bottom of stage settings (`Off` / `Only these runners` / `All except these runners`): dispatch, direct claims, and merge leases refuse ineligible Runners loudly while unrestricted stages behave exactly as before (task a3753643).
- Runner model auto-detect for every supported harness (pi, muse, antigravity, vibe, plus honest-empty opencode/codex legs) with per-harness counts and the first leg warning in Settings › Runners next to Re-detect, driven by the existing refresh command (task 2cbe91b6).
- Runner harness auto-detect now probes beyond PATH — standard install dirs (`~/.local/bin`, `~/bin`), each harness's own install dir, `KAINBAIN_*_BIN` overrides, and pi via its `~/.pi/agent` `models.json` snapshot — matching the backend's `discoverHarnesses`, so hosts with an SDK-only pi install (e.g. server2, whose service PATH lacks `~/.pi/agent/bin`) now detect pi and advertise its models in the fleet picker (task 2cbe91b6).
- Runner model discovery fails loud instead of reporting silent zeros: empty pi/muse scans record classified `PI_MODELS_EMPTY` / `MUSE_MSP_*` reasons with fixes in Settings, and re-detection names detected-but-unconfigured harnesses (`harness auto-detect also sees: …`) so a stale harness pin can no longer hide models; new installs record `auto` so every boot re-detects (task 2cbe91b6).
- Per-pipeline base branch: each named workflow can treat a feature branch as its main branch (pipeline settings `Base branch` field, blank = repo default) — new task branches fork off it, the merge stage merges back into it (and pushes it), CI `primary` mode runs on it, and review diffs compare against it; the base is pinned per task at creation so re-pointing a pipeline never retargets in-flight work, and a missing base is auto-created from the repo default tip (task cf4b6847).

### Changed

- Central queue across all pipelines/projects: both dispatch paths (embedded scheduler and runner fleet) and the queue display now sort through one shared seam in `oldest-first` mode by default — the oldest waiting task runs next wherever it lives, with furthest-along as a percentage of its own pipeline as tiebreak — so waiting work on a pipeline you are not viewing no longer starves behind late-stage work on the focused one; the follow-on pass can no longer pre-empt work waiting past the starvation ceiling (built-in 15 min, `KAINBAIN_DISPATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS`), `GET /tasks/queue` without `?projectId=` returns the all-projects queue instead of the UI-focused project, and the queue popup shows per-project waiting counts plus the current worker. Rollback: `KAINBAIN_CENTRAL_QUEUE_ORDER=furthest-along` (task 16d6fbd6).
- Task surfaces read easier: card titles render larger and semibold with the status as a chip (colour dot plus text label), details-tab banner text steps up to body size, and long audit logs preview behind a Show all disclosure (task e3369ccb).
- Runner model precedence stays pin-wins by default (pinned installs skip discovery and advertise exactly their pin across updates); `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1` opts in to survey-q4 discovery-wins, where a non-empty auto-detect result replaces the pin (task 2cbe91b6).
- Consolidated root-level markdown files into `docs/`: moved `CI_SCRIPTS.md`, `PORTABLE_DEPLOYMENT.md`, `agent-docs/`, and `research/phase0-branch-dry-run.md`; deleted 13 obsolete one-off summaries and superseded phase-2 plans (task fc3acfff).
- Merged the ALL / FAILED / HUMAN ONLY board pills into the unified search bar as `!` system filters (e.g. `auth #Dev !failed`): same dropdown, chips, and Any/All toggle as `#` tags; unknown `!tokens` stay as text; future native filters register via `frontend/src/components/workflow/systemFilters/` (task c213d3a9).

### Fixed

- Runners pick up waiting work on every pipeline, not just the viewed one: dispatch and direct claims now resolve each task's stage from its own pipeline instead of the active pipeline's stages, so a task on a non-active pipeline is matched against its own harness/model/tier/stage instead of being excluded or mis-served; tasks pointing at deleted stages park instead of running as another stage's job, and the pipeline switcher/toast now say "viewing" so the viewed pipeline no longer reads as the only live one (task 55460086).
- Stale Runner pins no longer pose as available models: the central model catalogue confirms every harness-scoped id against the claimant's own successful scans and marks contradicted ids unavailable with the stale-pin reason and claimant list (still shown in their section, never hidden); inconclusive signals (failed scans, old Runners, legacy/bare ids) keep trusting the advertisement, and dispatch refuses contradicted pins like unoffered models instead of routing work where the harness menu proved them absent — while the operator's `availableModels` override keeps its explicit say everywhere (task 9d2b75a2).
- Newly released harness models are selectable automatically: pinned Runners (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS`/`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL`) now still run model auto-discovery and advertise pin ∪ discovered ids (`modelSource: "pinned+discovered"`), so a brand-new model (e.g. a fresh Muse release) reaches the central model catalogue and every picker without editing the pin — the pin itself is never dropped; the muse discovery probe also passes `--provider` like the backend MSP catalogue so both read the host identically (task 9d2b75a2).
- Runner fleet cards stay named on every pipeline page: `GET /runners/monitor` now carries each assignment's own project/task/stage identity, the widget renders it even when the viewer looks at another pipeline, and "Open task" jumps to the job in its pipeline (task 350ca162).
- Bottom-bar queue number counts only tasks waiting to be picked up (never running, blocked, paused, failed, cancelled, or waiting-human tasks), and the queue popup lists exactly that same set in dispatch order (task 6d3c9317).
- Survey answers survive later Runner stages: Runner task-file shipments merge into the backend survey (new rounds land, saved answers are kept) instead of overwriting them with stale worktree copies; the question-me prompt also names the exact backend-resolved file for alias/extension-less configs (task fbcaef1d).
- Bottom (now-playing) bar on mobile is horizontally scrollable, so all runners are reachable instead of only the first (task a654a254).
- Pipeline releases published from the deploy tip worktree are synced back to the primary `dist/` and verified there; a stranded release now fails Publish loudly, and the Update stage verifies the installed commit against the last-publish pointer instead of reporting "already current" (task a654a254).
- Bottom (now-playing) bar stays live with no page refresh: runner boxes follow stage/task changes within one 5s fleet poll (all fleet surfaces share a single poller), and the queue chip refreshes within about a second of task activity with a 15s safety poll; background tabs pause polling and catch up on return (task ed00c209).
- Remote runners now self-update reliably: version selection is compatibility-gated (newest release whose manifest `requires.backendApi` admits the backend, never past it), the backend advertises its update directive and auto-nudges outdated command-capable runners daily, releases are cut by the publish pipeline instead of manual tags, and systemd installs boot through the self-update wrapper (with a migration script plus a read-only `doctor` for triage); see `docs/runner-update-runbook.md` (task 82e49a05).
- Stage prompts no longer name phantom reports: `# Previous Reports` (and `{{previousReports}}` / `{{latestReport*}}`) enumerate the files actually present in `docs/tasks/<taskId>/` — newest first, capped at `KAINBAIN_TASK_REPORTS_MAX_PROMPT_REFS` (default 5) with an overflow pointer, plus an explicit none-yet line for empty folders — so history entries whose file is gone are omitted instead of presented as available; report metadata keeps those entries flagged `missingOnDisk` for API/UI consumers (task 4f927ecb).
- Runner commit/hook failures are now visible and actionable: a refused commit (e.g. the pre-commit binary guard rejecting corrupt PNGs) reports as a failed completion with structured detail instead of dying in the runner journal, the task shows a "Commit Failed" callout (hook, command, affected files, remedy, full output) replacing the stale error, and the runner stays alive instead of crash-looping; after three consecutive same-signature failures the task parks (auto-dispatch and direct claims skip it) until an operator retries, resumes, or moves it (task 1cae113f).

# Changelog

All notable changes to KainBain are recorded here in **curated** form. The
per-commit baked history that backs the in-app **Changelog** dialog is generated
by `scripts/generate-changelog.mjs` and served through `GET /deploy/changelog`
(`frontend/src/components/layout/ChangelogModal.jsx`); it remains the exhaustive
source of truth. This file intentionally lists only high-impact changes.

## Update discipline

- Entries are curated **only at release time**, from the `Unreleased` section
  below, when a version tag/deploy is cut. Ordinary PRs are not required to touch
  this file (WP-10, task `8e61e197-cf8a-475e-b330-8cd7fa5a7e30`).
- Keep entries to one line each, grouped under `Added` / `Changed` / `Fixed` /
  `Removed` / `Security`. Reference the PR or task id in parentheses when
  helpful. Do not copy auto-generated commit subjects verbatim.
- After a release, rename the `## [Unreleased]` content to `## [x.y.z] -
  YYYY-MM-DD`.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Separate docs repo per project (stealth mode): a project can keep ALL KainBain information (task docs, plans, reports, and the `.kainbain/` state incl. `project.json`) in a private git repo instead of the main repo, which then stays completely free of KainBain traces. Offered under an Advanced disclosure on project create/import and in Project Settings → Files & Repositories; stored redacted, one docs repo per project (409 on re-claim); runners check the docs repo out adjacent to the main repo with synced `kb/<taskId>` branches and push docs first at stage handoff (task 7f6220c3).

- System Settings gains an About tab (also at `#/system-settings/about`) showing the running UI, backend, and screen-to-server API versions with per-row update guides, a warning banner when a newer release is advertised, and the latest security report summary with a full-report link — all served by the new `GET /status/versions` endpoint. The API row ties the UI-reported contract (`frontend/version.json`) to the backend contract (`api/version.json`) with a compatibility verdict (the same API major stays compatible across asymmetric redeploys, with an alert on mismatch); unadvertised latest-release knobs (`KAINBAIN_LATEST_*_VERSION`) report Up to date, while a missing security report file (`KAINBAIN_SECURITY_REPORT_PATH`) still shows the honest "no security report recorded" state (task c5c465c4).

- Runner model precedence stays pin-wins by default (pinned installs skip discovery and advertise exactly their pin across updates); `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1` opts in to survey-q4 discovery-wins, where a non-empty auto-detect result replaces the pin (task 2cbe91b6).
