- Merged the ALL / FAILED / HUMAN ONLY board pills into the unified search bar as `!` system filters (e.g. `auth #Dev !failed`): same dropdown, chips, and Any/All toggle as `#` tags; unknown `!tokens` stay as text; future native filters register via `frontend/src/components/workflow/systemFilters/` (task c213d3a9).

### Fixed

- Runners pick up waiting work on every pipeline, not just the viewed one: dispatch and direct claims now resolve each task's stage from its own pipeline instead of the active pipeline's stages, so a task on a non-active pipeline is matched against its own harness/model/tier/stage instead of being excluded or mis-served; tasks pointing at deleted stages park instead of running as another stage's job, and the pipeline switcher/toast now say "viewing" so the viewed pipeline no longer reads as the only live one (task 55460086).
- Stale Runner pins no longer pose as available models: the central model catalogue confirms every harness-scoped id against the claimant's own successful scans and marks contradicted ids unavailable with the stale-pin reason and claimant list (still shown in their section, never hidden); inconclusive signals (failed scans, old Runners, legacy/bare ids) keep trusting the advertisement, and dispatch refuses contradicted pins like unoffered models instead of routing work where the harness menu proved them absent — while the operator's `availableModels` override keeps its explicit say everywhere (task 9d2b75a2).
- Newly released harness models are selectable automatically: pinned Runners (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS`/`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL`) now still run model auto-discovery and advertise pin ∪ discovered ids (`modelSource: "pinned+discovered"`), so a brand-new model (e.g. a fresh Muse release) reaches the central model catalogue and every picker without editing the pin — the pin itself is never dropped; the muse discovery probe also passes `--provider` like the backend MSP catalogue so both read the host identically (task 9d2b75a2).
- Runner fleet cards stay named on every pipeline page: `GET /runners/monitor` now carries each assignment's own project/task/stage identity, the widget renders it even when the viewer looks at another pipeline, and "Open task" jumps to the job in its pipeline (task 350ca162).
- Bottom-bar queue number counts only tasks waiting to be picked up (never running, blocked, paused, failed, cancelled, or waiting-human tasks), and the queue popup lists exactly that same set in dispatch order (task 6d3c9317).
- Survey answers survive later Runner stages: Runner task-file shipments merge into the backend survey (new rounds land, saved answers are kept) instead of overwriting them with stale worktree copies; the question-me prompt also names the exact backend-resolved file for alias/extension-less configs (task fbcaef1d).
- Bottom (now-playing) bar on mobile is horizontally scrollable, so all runners are reachable instead of only the first (task a654a254).
- Pipeline releases published from the deploy tip worktree are synced back to the primary `dist/` and verified there; a stranded release now fails Publish loudly, and the Update stage verifies the installed commit against the last-publish pointer instead of reporting "already current" (task a654a254).
- Bottom (now-playing) bar stays live with no page refresh: runner boxes follow stage/task changes within one 5s fleet poll (all fleet surfaces share a single poller), and the queue chip refreshes within about a second of task activity with a 15s safety poll; background tabs pause polling and catch up on return (task ed00c209).
- Remote runners now self-update reliably: version selection is compatibility-gated (newest release whose manifest `requires.backendApi` admits the backend, never past it), the backend advertises its update directive and auto-nudges outdated command-capable runners daily, releases are cut by the publish pipeline instead of manual tags, and systemd installs boot through the self-update wrapper (with a migration script plus a read-only `doctor` for triage); see `docs/runner-update-runbook.md` (task 82e49a05).
- Stage prompts no longer name phantom reports: `# Previous Reports` (and `{{previousReports}}` / `{{latestReport*}}`) enumerate the files actually present in `docs/tasks/<taskId>/` — newest first, capped at `KAINBAIN_TASK_REPORTS_MAX_PROMPT_REFS` (default 5) with an overflow pointer, plus an explicit none-yet line for empty folders — so history entries whose file is gone are omitted instead of presented as available; report metadata keeps those entries flagged `missingOnDisk` for API/UI consumers (task 4f927ecb).
- Runner commit/hook failures are now visible and actionable: a refused commit (e.g. the pre-commit binary guard rejecting corrupt PNGs) reports as a failed completion with structured detail instead of dying in the runner journal, the task shows a "Commit Failed" callout (hook, command, affected files, remedy, full output) replacing the stale error, and the runner stays alive instead of crash-looping; after three consecutive same-signature failures the task parks (auto-dispatch and direct claims skip it) until an operator retries, resumes, or moves it (task 1cae113f).

--- CHANGELOG
# Changelog

All notable changes to KainBain are recorded here in **curated** form. The
per-commit baked history that backs the in-app **Changelog** dialog is generated
by `scripts/generate-changelog.mjs` and served through `GET /deploy/changelog`
(`frontend/src/components/layout/ChangelogModal.jsx`); it remains the exhaustive
source of truth. This file intentionally lists only high-impact changes.

## Update discipline

- Entries are curated **only at release time**, from the `Unreleased` section
  below, when a version tag/deploy is cut. Ordinary PRs are not required to touch
  this file (WP-10, task `8e61e197-cf8a-475e-b330-8cd7fa5a7e30`).
- Keep entries to one line each, grouped under `Added` / `Changed` / `Fixed` /
  `Removed` / `Security`. Reference the PR or task id in parentheses when
  helpful. Do not copy auto-generated commit subjects verbatim.
- After a release, rename the `## [Unreleased]` content to `## [x.y.z] -
  YYYY-MM-DD`.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Separate docs repo per project (stealth mode): a project can keep ALL KainBain information (task docs, plans, reports, and the `.kainbain/` state incl. `project.json`) in a private git repo instead of the main repo, which then stays completely free of KainBain traces. Offered under an Advanced disclosure on project create/import and in Project Settings → Files & Repositories; stored redacted, one docs repo per project (409 on re-claim); runners check the docs repo out adjacent to the main repo with synced `kb/<taskId>` branches and push docs first at stage handoff (task 7f6220c3).

- System Settings gains an About tab (also at `#/system-settings/about`) showing the running UI, backend, and screen-to-server API versions with per-row update guides, a warning banner when a newer release is advertised, and the latest security report summary with a full-report link — all served by the new `GET /status/versions` endpoint. The API row ties the UI-reported contract (`frontend/version.json`) to the backend contract (`api/version.json`) with a compatibility verdict (the same API major stays compatible across asymmetric redeploys, with an alert on mismatch); unadvertised latest-release knobs (`KAINBAIN_LATEST_*_VERSION`) report Up to date, while a missing security report file (`KAINBAIN_SECURITY_REPORT_PATH`) still shows the honest "no security report recorded" state (task c5c465c4).

- Task goals render ` ```mermaid ` fences as inline SVG diagrams in the markdown viewer (mermaid lazy-loads only when a diagram is present and sanitizes at `strict` security level; a broken or unrenderable diagram degrades to its readable source block, never a blank hole), and the `creating-new-tickets` skill now drafts each ticket as its own markdown file under the task directory's `drafts/` folder before POSTing the file's exact contents, so API-created tickets land as structured documents (headings, steps, code, diagrams, image refs) instead of paragraphs; the first-line title, `blockedBy` validation, idempotency, and dedupe behave exactly as before (task 5a38ad45).

- Stage+config attestation for compliance proof: every per-stage wrap-up commit and its stage-history entry now carry the same task+stage config hash (git trailers plus a durable prose token with the commit SHA), verifiable offline with `node scripts/verify-stage-attestation.mjs --repo <path> --task <id>` (see the Stage Attestation site-docs article); clean-tree stages attest with an explicit null commit, and entries predating the feature stay valid without hashes (task d20f0c83).

- API key system for agents and external services (off by default, separate `KAINBAIN_API_KEYS_ENABLED` switch): admin-managed keys with catalogue roles plus narrowing scopes, secret shown once and stored hashed, task mutations gated per key grant, every key action flagged by key name in task history and the audit log, and a per-key usage view — browser sessions and Runners work unchanged with the switch on or off (task ac988ba8).
- Docs article `h2` sections collapse and expand via their headers (chevron toggle, keyboard-operable, Expand all / Collapse all above the article), and headers render larger and bolder for scanning (task e3369ccb).
- Task detail pages and `GET /tasks/:id` now show where a task works (branch, workspace-isolation mode, worktree path) via the additive `workingLocation` field, and a new `Develop Alongside KainBain` site-docs article teaches the pause-edit-resume, separate-branch, and review-gate flows; dirty-tree guard errors now name the blocking paths plus the safe next step for hand edits (task 8dafdce1).
- Per-stage Runner allow/block list at the bottom of stage settings (`Off` / `Only these runners` / `All except these runners`): dispatch, direct claims, and merge leases refuse ineligible Runners loudly while unrestricted stages behave exactly as before (task a3753643).
- Runner model auto-detect for every supported harness (pi, muse, antigravity, vibe, plus honest-empty opencode/codex legs) with per-harness counts and the first leg warning in Settings › Runners next to Re-detect, driven by the existing refresh command (task 2cbe91b6).
- Runner harness auto-detect now probes beyond PATH — standard install dirs (`~/.local/bin`, `~/bin`), each harness's own install dir, `KAINBAIN_*_BIN` overrides, and pi via its `~/.pi/agent` `models.json` snapshot — matching the backend's `discoverHarnesses`, so hosts with an SDK-only pi install (e.g. server2, whose service PATH lacks `~/.pi/agent/bin`) now detect pi and advertise its models in the fleet picker (task 2cbe91b6).
- Runner model discovery fails loud instead of reporting silent zeros: empty pi/muse scans record classified `PI_MODELS_EMPTY` / `MUSE_MSP_*` reasons with fixes in Settings, and re-detection names detected-but-unconfigured harnesses (`harness auto-detect also sees: …`) so a stale harness pin can no longer hide models; new installs record `auto` so every boot re-detects (task 2cbe91b6).
- Per-pipeline base branch: each named workflow can treat a feature branch as its main branch (pipeline settings `Base branch` field, blank = repo default) — new task branches fork off it, the merge stage merges back into it (and pushes it), CI `primary` mode runs on it, and review diffs compare against it; the base is pinned per task at creation so re-pointing a pipeline never retargets in-flight work, and a missing base is auto-created from the repo default tip (task cf4b6847).

### Changed

- Central queue across all pipelines/projects: both dispatch paths (embedded scheduler and runner fleet) and the queue display now sort through one shared seam in `oldest-first` mode by default — the oldest waiting task runs next wherever it lives, with furthest-along as a percentage of its own pipeline as tiebreak — so waiting work on a pipeline you are not viewing no longer starves behind late-stage work on the focused one; the follow-on pass can no longer pre-empt work waiting past the starvation ceiling (built-in 15 min, `KAINBAIN_DISPATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS`), `GET /tasks/queue` without `?projectId=` returns the all-projects queue instead of the UI-focused project, and the queue popup shows per-project waiting counts plus the current worker. Rollback: `KAINBAIN_CENTRAL_QUEUE_ORDER=furthest-along` (task 16d6fbd6).
- Task surfaces read easier: card titles render larger and semibold with the status as a chip (colour dot plus text label), details-tab banner text steps up to body size, and long audit logs preview behind a Show all disclosure (task e3369ccb).
- Runner model precedence stays pin-wins by default (pinned installs skip discovery and advertise exactly their pin across updates); `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1` opts in to survey-q4 discovery-wins, where a non-empty auto-detect result replaces the pin (task 2cbe91b6).
- Consolidated root-level markdown files into `docs/`: moved `CI_SCRIPTS.md`, `PORTABLE_DEPLOYMENT.md`, `agent-docs/`, and `research/phase0-branch-dry-run.md`; deleted 13 obsolete one-off summaries and superseded phase-2 plans (task fc3acfff).
- Merged the ALL / FAILED / HUMAN ONLY board pills into the unified search bar as `!` system filters (e.g. `auth #Dev !failed`): same dropdown, chips, and Any/All toggle as `#` tags; unknown `!tokens` stay as text; future native filters register via `frontend/src/components/workflow/systemFilters/` (task c213d3a9).

### Fixed

- Runners pick up waiting work on every pipeline, not just the viewed one: dispatch and direct claims now resolve each task's stage from its own pipeline instead of the active pipeline's stages, so a task on a non-active pipeline is matched against its own harness/model/tier/stage instead of being excluded or mis-served; tasks pointing at deleted stages park instead of running as another stage's job, and the pipeline switcher/toast now say "viewing" so the viewed pipeline no longer reads as the only live one (task 55460086).
- Stale Runner pins no longer pose as available models: the central model catalogue confirms every harness-scoped id against the claimant's own successful scans and marks contradicted ids unavailable with the stale-pin reason and claimant list (still shown in their section, never hidden); inconclusive signals (failed scans, old Runners, legacy/bare ids) keep trusting the advertisement, and dispatch refuses contradicted pins like unoffered models instead of routing work where the harness menu proved them absent — while the operator's `availableModels` override keeps its explicit say everywhere (task 9d2b75a2).
- Newly released harness models are selectable automatically: pinned Runners (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS`/`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL`) now still run model auto-discovery and advertise pin ∪ discovered ids (`modelSource: "pinned+discovered"`), so a brand-new model (e.g. a fresh Muse release) reaches the central model catalogue and every picker without editing the pin — the pin itself is never dropped; the muse discovery probe also passes `--provider` like the backend MSP catalogue so both read the host identically (task 9d2b75a2).
- Runner fleet cards stay named on every pipeline page: `GET /runners/monitor` now carries each assignment's own project/task/stage identity, the widget renders it even when the viewer looks at another pipeline, and "Open task" jumps to the job in its pipeline (task 350ca162).
- Bottom-bar queue number counts only tasks waiting to be picked up (never running, blocked, paused, failed, cancelled, or waiting-human tasks), and the queue popup lists exactly that same set in dispatch order (task 6d3c9317).
- Survey answers survive later Runner stages: Runner task-file shipments merge into the backend survey (new rounds land, saved answers are kept) instead of overwriting them with stale worktree copies; the question-me prompt also names the exact backend-resolved file for alias/extension-less configs (task fbcaef1d).
- Bottom (now-playing) bar on mobile is horizontally scrollable, so all runners are reachable instead of only the first (task a654a254).
- Pipeline releases published from the deploy tip worktree are synced back to the primary `dist/` and verified there; a stranded release now fails Publish loudly, and the Update stage verifies the installed commit against the last-publish pointer instead of reporting "already current" (task a654a254).
- Bottom (now-playing) bar stays live with no page refresh: runner boxes follow stage/task changes within one 5s fleet poll (all fleet surfaces share a single poller), and the queue chip refreshes within about a second of task activity with a 15s safety poll; background tabs pause polling and catch up on return (task ed00c209).
- Remote runners now self-update reliably: version selection is compatibility-gated (newest release whose manifest `requires.backendApi` admits the backend, never past it), the backend advertises its update directive and auto-nudges outdated command-capable runners daily, releases are cut by the publish pipeline instead of manual tags, and systemd installs boot through the self-update wrapper (with a migration script plus a read-only `doctor` for triage); see `docs/runner-update-runbook.md` (task 82e49a05).
- Stage prompts no longer name phantom reports: `# Previous Reports` (and `{{previousReports}}` / `{{latestReport*}}`) enumerate the files actually present in `docs/tasks/<taskId>/` — newest first, capped at `KAINBAIN_TASK_REPORTS_MAX_PROMPT_REFS` (default 5) with an overflow pointer, plus an explicit none-yet line for empty folders — so history entries whose file is gone are omitted instead of presented as available; report metadata keeps those entries flagged `missingOnDisk` for API/UI consumers (task 4f927ecb).
- Runner commit/hook failures are now visible and actionable: a refused commit (e.g. the pre-commit binary guard rejecting corrupt PNGs) reports as a failed completion with structured detail instead of dying in the runner journal, the task shows a "Commit Failed" callout (hook, command, affected files, remedy, full output) replacing the stale error, and the runner stays alive instead of crash-looping; after three consecutive same-signature failures the task parks (auto-dispatch and direct claims skip it) until an operator retries, resumes, or moves it (task 1cae113f).

pinned key in `runner/updates/verify.js`, and installs the newest release
that is strictly newer, not a pre-release, and compatible with the backend
it talks to (each manifest's `requires.backendApi` range must admit the
backend API version learned from heartbeats; unknown backend versions
stay ungated). It verifies the asset sha256, atomically flips `current`
to the new tree (keeping `previous` for rollback), and exits 0 so the
wrapper restarts it. When latest verifies but is incompatible, the GitHub
path walks one bounded releases-list page (30 entries, newest-first) for
the newest older release that qualifies. Direct
`node runner/main.js` is dev-only: it stages updates but cannot restart
itself. New knobs:

- `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_UPDATE_URL` — release pointer override for air-gapped
  mirrors (a base serving `manifest.json` + `.minisig` + assets plus an
  optional `releases.json` index for multi-release selection, or a full
  `manifest.json` URL as an explicit single-candidate pin). Default is
  the GitHub `releases/latest` API.
- `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` — opt out of self-update checks.
- `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_UPDATE_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS` — poll base in ms (default
  3600000, min 300000; ±20% jitter).
- `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT` — install root holding
  `releases/`, `current`, `previous`, `update-state.json` (default:
  `runner-install` sibling of the work root).

A 409 `RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM` from dispatch/claim means the backend
floor moved past this Runner: it self-updates immediately (when idle,
bypassing the check interval) and retries. Tampered assets/manifests abort
the update, keep the old version, and surface an "update failed" badge in
Settings › Runners via the next heartbeat. Any apply failure (network cut
mid-download, busy updater, missing `tar`) is contained the same way: the
loop backs off and keeps serving the old version, never crashing. Hung
mirrors time out (30s pointer/manifest, 5 min assets). Windows hosts are
not supported in v1 (linux/darwin × x64/arm64). Operator procedures
(release cutting, rollback, wrapper migration, "says out of date"
triage) live in `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`.

## On-request commands (ADR 0013)

Settings › Runners can nudge this daemon through the heartbeat pull channel:
Re-detect models re-runs model discovery promptly for every configured
harness (bypassing the 12h gate once; acked as
`discovered N model(s) (pi:12, muse:3)` with the first leg error code
when a leg fails, cache kept; a Runner with no legged harness acks
`discovered 0 model(s) (no discovery legs configured)`; skipped with
a `models pinned` ack when the operator pinned models, unless
`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1` opts in to discovery-wins)
and Update now queues an idle-only self-update. Both ride
`pendingCommands` on the heartbeat response and ack via `facts.commandAck`;
a queued command waits for the next heartbeat, and Update now never
interrupts live work — it applies at the next idle point. Older daemons
that predate `facts.commands` ignore the channel; Settings shows manual
guidance instead of a dead button.

## Build identity and stale-code detection

Every heartbeat reports `versions.build` (`{ sha, builtAt, dirty, source }`),
`versions.bootedAtMs`, and `versions.codeChangedSinceBoot`:

- Packaged Runners carry the release stamp (`source: "package"`): the
  commit, bundle time, and tree dirtiness recorded by
  `scripts/package-runner.mjs` at bundle time.
- Dev Runners booted from a git checkout compute it at boot instead
  (`source: "checkout"`): `git rev-parse HEAD` plus dirty from
  `git status --porcelain` scoped to `runner/`. No bundle time exists for
  a live checkout, so `builtAt` is null. Outside a checkout with no stamp
  every field is null ("unknown") — never a boot failure.
- At boot the daemon fingerprints its own `runner/` tree (file count,
  bytes, newest mtime); each heartbeat rescans cheaply and reports
  `codeChangedSinceBoot: true` once any file changes underneath the
  running process (edits, added/removed files). `.git` and
  `node_modules` are never scanned.

Settings › Runners shows the short sha next to the version badge and warns
(warn-only, never a block) when the code changed after boot or when the
build sha differs from the backend commit. Dev checkouts show their build
info but never warn. Old Runners without build identity show "unknown"
with no warning, and old backends ignore the new `versions` keys.

## Upgrade note: the backend now requires projectId on every write (WP1 tenant fence)

If you run the workers, this is the one upgrade note that affects you.

**Symptom after upgrading the backend.** An old Runner (one that predates
this change) starts failing its writes with either of these errors:

- `400 MISSING_PROJECT_ID` — the Runner sent a progress / logs /
  completion / heartbeat / ack report without naming its project. Before
  this change the backend guessed the active project; it no longer does.
- `409 PROJECT_FENCE_MISMATCH` — the Runner replayed a lease (execution
  id + epoch) against a different project than the one that issued it.
  The original lease is untouched; only the replayed write is rejected.

**Action.** Upgrade the Runner to this version (or newer) and restart it.
Current Runners already send `projectId` with every write, so once both
sides are upgraded there is nothing to configure.

**No data migration.** Leases live in backend memory only — there is
nothing to convert, backfill, or re-issue. In-flight work leases simply
re-queue as interrupted across the backend restart, exactly like any
other restart, and pick up fresh leases on the next dispatch poll.

pinned key in `runner/updates/verify.js`, and installs the newest release
that is strictly newer, not a pre-release, and compatible with the backend
it talks to (each manifest's `requires.backendApi` range must admit the
backend API version learned from heartbeats; unknown backend versions
stay ungated). It verifies the asset sha256, atomically flips `current`
to the new tree (keeping `previous` for rollback), and exits 0 so the
wrapper restarts it. When latest verifies but is incompatible, the GitHub
path walks one bounded releases-list page (30 entries, newest-first) for
the newest older release that qualifies. Direct
`node runner/main.js` is dev-only: it stages updates but cannot restart
itself. New knobs:

- `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_UPDATE_URL` — release pointer override for air-gapped
  mirrors (a base serving `manifest.json` + `.minisig` + assets plus an
  optional `releases.json` index for multi-release selection, or a full
  `manifest.json` URL as an explicit single-candidate pin). Default is
  the GitHub `releases/latest` API.
- `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` — opt out of self-update checks.
- `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_UPDATE_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS` — poll base in ms (default
  3600000, min 300000; ±20% jitter).
- `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT` — install root holding
  `releases/`, `current`, `previous`, `update-state.json` (default:
  `runner-install` sibling of the work root).

A 409 `RUNNER_VERSION_BELOW_MINIMUM` from dispatch/claim means the backend
floor moved past this Runner: it self-updates immediately (when idle,
bypassing the check interval) and retries. Tampered assets/manifests abort
the update, keep the old version, and surface an "update failed" badge in
Settings › Runners via the next heartbeat. Any apply failure (network cut
mid-download, busy updater, missing `tar`) is contained the same way: the
loop backs off and keeps serving the old version, never crashing. Hung
mirrors time out (30s pointer/manifest, 5 min assets). Windows hosts are
not supported in v1 (linux/darwin × x64/arm64). Operator procedures
(release cutting, rollback, wrapper migration, "says out of date"
triage) live in `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`.

## On-request commands (ADR 0013)

Settings › Runners can nudge this daemon through the heartbeat pull channel:
Re-detect models re-runs model discovery promptly for every configured
harness (bypassing the 12h gate once; acked as
`discovered N model(s) (pi:12, muse:3)` with the first leg error code
when a leg fails, cache kept; a Runner with no legged harness acks
`discovered 0 model(s) (no discovery legs configured)`; skipped with
a `models pinned` ack when the operator pinned models, unless
`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1` opts in to discovery-wins)
and Update now queues an idle-only self-update. Both ride
`pendingCommands` on the heartbeat response and ack via `facts.commandAck`;
a queued command waits for the next heartbeat, and Update now never
interrupts live work — it applies at the next idle point. Older daemons
that predate `facts.commands` ignore the channel; Settings shows manual
guidance instead of a dead button.

## Build identity and stale-code detection

Every heartbeat reports `versions.build` (`{ sha, builtAt, dirty, source }`),
`versions.bootedAtMs`, and `versions.codeChangedSinceBoot`:

- Packaged Runners carry the release stamp (`source: "package"`): the
  commit, bundle time, and tree dirtiness recorded by
  `scripts/package-runner.mjs` at bundle time.
- Dev Runners booted from a git checkout compute it at boot instead
  (`source: "checkout"`): `git rev-parse HEAD` plus dirty from
  `git status --porcelain` scoped to `runner/`. No bundle time exists for
  a live checkout, so `builtAt` is null. Outside a checkout with no stamp
  every field is null ("unknown") — never a boot failure.
- At boot the daemon fingerprints its own `runner/` tree (file count,
  bytes, newest mtime); each heartbeat rescans cheaply and reports
  `codeChangedSinceBoot: true` once any file changes underneath the
  running process (edits, added/removed files). `.git` and
  `node_modules` are never scanned.

Settings › Runners shows the short sha next to the version badge and warns
(warn-only, never a block) when the code changed after boot or when the
build sha differs from the backend commit. Dev checkouts show their build
info but never warn. Old Runners without build identity show "unknown"
with no warning, and old backends ignore the new `versions` keys.

## Upgrade note: the backend now requires projectId on every write (WP1 tenant fence)

If you run the workers, this is the one upgrade note that affects you.

**Symptom after upgrading the backend.** An old Runner (one that predates
this change) starts failing its writes with either of these errors:

- `400 MISSING_PROJECT_ID` — the Runner sent a progress / logs /
  completion / heartbeat / ack report without naming its project. Before
  this change the backend guessed the active project; it no longer does.
- `409 PROJECT_FENCE_MISMATCH` — the Runner replayed a lease (execution
  id + epoch) against a different project than the one that issued it.
  The original lease is untouched; only the replayed write is rejected.

**Action.** Upgrade the Runner to this version (or newer) and restart it.
Current Runners already send `projectId` with every write, so once both
sides are upgraded there is nothing to configure.

**No data migration.** Leases live in backend memory only — there is
nothing to convert, backfill, or re-issue. In-flight work leases simply
re-queue as interrupted across the backend restart, exactly like any
other restart, and pick up fresh leases on the next dispatch poll.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — record the fleet matrix
# (GET /runners + GET /deploy/status) and a per-runner convergence verdict.
# READ-ONLY against the backend; safe to run any time, any number of times.
#
# Outputs in <outdir>:
#   runners-<stamp>.json        raw GET /runners payload (evidence)
#   runners-<stamp>.tsv         flat fleet table incl. build sha/builtAt
#   deploy-status-<stamp>.json  raw GET /deploy/status payload
#   verdict-<stamp>.txt         one line per named runner: CONVERGED or the reasons why not
#
# Convergence rule (S5 success criterion 1): runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the
# running build's reported git sha contains the fix commit — verified locally
# with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fixCommit> <buildSha>`, because a version
# string alone cannot prove which code is running. If the runner reports no
# build sha, the verdict says so instead of guessing.
#
# Knobs (env):
#   KAINBAIN_API_BASE            default http://192.168.1.206:3100
#   KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS    default "local-alpha,server2-alpha"
#   KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT       default 046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4 (the 046a6391 deterministic-git-failure change)
#
# Exit codes: 0 snapshot written (converged or not — read verdict-<stamp>.txt);
#   1 setup or API failure (nothing trustworthy written);
#   3 snapshot written, --require-converged given, but not all named runners converged.
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

# fix_in_build <buildSha|""|null> — prints true/false/null. null = cannot tell
# (no sha reported, or sha unknown to the local repo). Uses the local Kainbain
# checkout as the commit database — read-only git queries only.
fix_in_build() {
  local sha="$1" repo_root="$2" fix_commit="$3"
  if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ "$sha" = "null" ]; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if ! git -C "$repo_root" cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if git -C "$repo_root" merge-base --is-ancestor "$fix_commit" "$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo true
  else
    echo false
  fi
}

# verdict_for <runners.json> <runnerId> — prints the verdict JSON object for one
# runner (jq/runner-verdict.jq + the git ancestry check).
verdict_for() {
  local runners_json="$1" runner_id="$2" repo_root="$3" fix_commit="$4"
  local runner sha fix
  runner="$(jq -c --arg id "$runner_id" '.[] | select(.runnerId == $id) // empty' "$runners_json")"

    return 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — record the fleet matrix
# (GET /runners + GET /deploy/status) and a per-runner convergence verdict.
# READ-ONLY against the backend; safe to run any time, any number of times.
#
# Outputs in <outdir>:
#   runners-<stamp>.json        raw GET /runners payload (evidence)
#   runners-<stamp>.tsv         flat fleet table incl. build sha/builtAt
#   deploy-status-<stamp>.json  raw GET /deploy/status payload
#   verdict-<stamp>.txt         one line per named runner: CONVERGED or the reasons why not
#
# Convergence rule (S5 success criterion 1): runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the
# running build's reported git sha contains the fix commit — verified locally
# with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fixCommit> <buildSha>`, because a version
# string alone cannot prove which code is running. If the runner reports no
# build sha, the verdict says so instead of guessing.
#
# Knobs (env):
#   KAINBAIN_API_BASE            default http://192.168.1.206:3100
#   KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS    default "local-alpha,server2-alpha"
#   KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT       default 046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4 (the 046a6391 deterministic-git-failure change)
#
# Exit codes: 0 snapshot written (converged or not — read verdict-<stamp>.txt);
#   1 setup or API failure (nothing trustworthy written);
#   3 snapshot written, --require-converged given, but not all named runners converged.
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

# fix_in_build <buildSha|""|null> — prints true/false/null. null = cannot tell
# (no sha reported, or sha unknown to the local repo). Uses the local Kainbain
# checkout as the commit database — read-only git queries only.
fix_in_build() {
  local sha="$1" repo_root="$2" fix_commit="$3"
  if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ "$sha" = "null" ]; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if ! git -C "$repo_root" cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if git -C "$repo_root" merge-base --is-ancestor "$fix_commit" "$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo true
  else
    echo false
  fi
}

# verdict_for <runners.json> <runnerId> — prints the verdict JSON object for one
# runner (jq/runner-verdict.jq + the git ancestry check).
verdict_for() {
  local runners_json="$1" runner_id="$2" repo_root="$3" fix_commit="$4"
  local runner sha fix
  runner="$(jq -c --arg id "$runner_id" '.[] | select(.runnerId == $id) // empty' "$runners_json")"
  if [ -z "$runner" ]; then
    printf '{"runnerId":"%s","converged":false,"reasons":["runner not present in GET /runners (offline/revoked?)"]}\n' "$runner_id"
    return 0
  fi

# Outputs in <outdir>:
#   runners-<stamp>.json        raw GET /runners payload (evidence)
#   runners-<stamp>.tsv         flat fleet table incl. build sha/builtAt
#   deploy-status-<stamp>.json  raw GET /deploy/status payload
#   verdict-<stamp>.txt         one line per named runner: CONVERGED or the reasons why not
#
# Convergence rule (S5 success criterion 1): runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the
# running build's reported git sha contains the fix commit — verified locally
# with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fixCommit> <buildSha>`, because a version
# string alone cannot prove which code is running. If the runner reports no
# build sha, the verdict says so instead of guessing.
#
# Knobs (env):
#   KAINBAIN_API_BASE            default http://192.168.1.206:3100
#   KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS    default "local-alpha,server2-alpha"

#
# Exit codes: 0 snapshot written (converged or not — read verdict-<stamp>.txt);
#   1 setup or API failure (nothing trustworthy written);
#   3 snapshot written, --require-converged given, but not all named runners converged.
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

# fix_in_build <buildSha|""|null> — prints true/false/null. null = cannot tell
# (no sha reported, or sha unknown to the local repo). Uses the local Kainbain
# checkout as the commit database — read-only git queries only.
fix_in_build() {
  local sha="$1" repo_root="$2" fix_commit="$3"
  if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ "$sha" = "null" ]; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if ! git -C "$repo_root" cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if git -C "$repo_root" merge-base --is-ancestor "$fix_commit" "$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo true
  else
    echo false
  fi
}

verdict_for() {

**Task:** `683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c` · **Date:** 2026-11-24

**Verdict: PASS — no install-breaking change found.** This file is the only file added this stage.

## 1. This branch introduces zero runtime changes

`git diff main...HEAD --name-only` lists only files under
`docs/tasks/683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c/` (recounts, snapshots, scripts
under that folder, `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `BASELINE.md`, etc.).
`git diff main...HEAD --name-only | grep -v '^docs/'` is empty, and a search for
`scripts/|runner/|api/|frontend/` in the diff is empty. No backend, runner,
installer, Docker, CI, or config file is touched, so `git pull` of this branch and
the runner self-update channel are unaffected by it. Observation scripts in
`bin/` are read-only by inspection and header comment: `fleet-recount.sh` (GETs
only, writes only under the task folder), `runners-snapshot.sh` (GETs only),
`e5-sweep.sh` (ls/git/log/for-each-ref/journalctl only, explicit "READ-ONLY: it
never reaps, deletes, restarts, updates, or modifies anything").

Hygiene note (not a break): `bin/tests/__pycache__/mock-api.cpython-314.pyc` is
tracked under docs/. It is never packaged into the runner bundle or backend
image (which ship `runner/` and `api/`, not `docs/`), so it cannot break installs.
Flagged for cleanup on the next task-folder touch, not a FAIL.

## 2. The 0.1.0 → 0.2.1 runner release this stage rolls out is backward compatible

Verified from the tags live on 2026-11-24:

- `runner/version.json` at `runner-v0.1.0`, `runner-v0.2.0`, `runner-v0.2.1` all
  declare `"requires": { "backendApi": ">=1.0.0 <2.0.0" }` and
  `api/version.json` accepts `runner >=1.0.0 <2.0.0` unchanged. The updater's
  compat gate therefore treats 0.2.1 as installable against the same backend;
  no new API floor was introduced.
- No runner source file is deleted between `runner-v0.1.0..runner-v0.2.1`
  (`--diff-filter=D` under `runner/` is empty; deletions are only old
  `docs/tasks/*/task.md` files). Install layout (`releases/`, `current`/`previous`
  symlinks, `update-state.json`) is unchanged, so existing
  `$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT` stays valid; the wrapper's new
  `doctor` subcommand and `restart-requested` sentinel are additive.
- New runner env vars all have safe defaults and are opt-outs, not requirements:
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_IMPROMPTU` defaults to `1` (opt out with `0`),
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_DISCOVERY_STALE_MS` defaults to `24h`,
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS` defaults to `0`. `.env.example` diff
  adds only additive knobs with defaults; `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` stay `0.1.0`. Existing env files boot unchanged.
- Wire changes are additive and tolerated both ways: `complete-execution` gains
  optional `gitFailure`/`configHash`/`committed` (`runner/client.js` spreads them
  only when present; old backends ignore unknown keys). New impromptu endpoints
  are only polled when the feature is enabled; the dispatch loop is unaffected.

1|# Runner update runbook
2|
3|Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
4|`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
5|rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
6|that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
7|serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.
8|
9|## Cutting a runner release (normal path)
10|
11|The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.
12|
13|1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
14|   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
15|   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
16|2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
17|   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
18|   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
19|   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
20|3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
21|4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
22|   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
23|   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
24|   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
25|   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
26|   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
27|5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
28|   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
29|   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
30|   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
31|   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
32|   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).
33|
34|## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)
35|
36|When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
37|hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:
38|
39|```
40|git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
41|git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
42|```
43|
44|Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
45|version forward instead.
46|
47|## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)
48|
49|1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
50|   resolves to the prior tag.
51|2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
52|   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
53|   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
54|3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
55|   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
56|   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
57|   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
58|4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
59|   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
60|   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
61|   is cut.
62|
63|Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
64|fleet converged.
65|
66|## Migrating a host to the wrapper
67|
68|Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
69|restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
70|versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
71|the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
72|so the fleet version does not change).
73|
74|Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:
75|
76|```
77|# 1. Pre-check (read-only, safe any time):
78|KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
79|  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service
80|
81|# 2. Rehearse:
82|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id> --dry-run
83|
84|# 3. Migrate (snapshots unit + env, reloads, restarts, re-verifies):
85|scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id>
86|```
87|
88|The script refuses to overwrite an existing `current` link and prints
89|revert commands (copy the `.bak-<timestamp>` files back, reload,
90|restart). New installs need no migration: both installers
91|(`scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `startRunner.sh`) already write
92|wrapper-based units. Verify after: `doctor` reports `status: ok` with
93|`entrypoint: wrapper`, and the next heartbeat shows the same version
94|as before.
95|
96|## Restart vs Update (Settings › Runners)
97|
98|Two separate actions, never combined:
99|
100|- **Restart** reboots the runner on its **current version** — no update
101|  check runs. It is destructive: any work running on that runner is
102|  stopped at once (the claim lease expires so the work re-queues, like a
103|  crash). The confirm window names the runner and warns about running
104|  work; use it when a runner looks stuck, not to change versions.
105|  Mechanism: the daemon writes a `restart-requested` sentinel beside the
106|  install root and exits 0; the wrapper consumes it and boots the SAME
107|  tree again. Restart therefore needs the wrapper entrypoint — a runner
108|  started as bare `node main.js` exits without rebooting (migrate to the
109|  wrapper, above).
110|- **Update** reinstalls the runner onto its **target version** — the
111|  exact pin when the runner is pinned, otherwise the newest compatible
112|  release — and applies only when the runner is idle (never interrupts
113|  work). A busy runner queues the update for the next idle point.
114|
115|## Per-runner version setting
116|
117|Each runner is set to **Latest** (default) or one exact release, via
118|the version dropdown on its Settings › Runners detail panel:
119|
120|- **Latest** tracks the newest release. It auto-updates at the next
121|  idle point (including right after a restart, once idle), and the
122|  backend nudges trailing runners at most daily. A red banner appears
123|  whenever a newer version exists than the one running — update (or
124|  wait for idle) to converge it.
125|- **Pinned** stays on exactly that release. Pinned runners never
126|  auto-update (no nudges, no idle installs, no restart-time installs);
127|  only the manual **Update** button installs the pin, and only when the
128|  pin is newer than the running version — the channel never downgrades,
129|  so a pin older than running shows a softer warning and the Update
130|  button stays disabled with the reason. Pick Latest or a newer pin to
131|  move forward.
132|
133|The dropdown lists Latest plus every fleet-known release (newest
134|first): each runner's running version plus the fleet recommended and
135|minimum knobs — offline-safe, no release catalogue fetch.
136|
137|## Triage: a runner says out of date
138|
139|Start on the runner host (or ask the host owner to run it) — the
140|doctor is read-only and never writes:
141|
142|```
143|$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service
144|```
145|
146|Match the Settings › Runners badge to a cause:
147|
148|- **"update available" that never clears.** The runner trails
149|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (Latest runners) or its pin.
150|  If the doctor says `entrypoint: direct`, migrate to the wrapper
151|  (above) — staged updates can never boot there. If the env shows
152|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` (or `(unset)` with a host-level
153|  opt-out), the runner acked the nudge with "skipped: auto-update is
154|  disabled" — flip that switch. If the runner is pinned, only the
155|  manual Update button installs (pins never auto-update); a pin older
156|  than running refuses with "never downgrades" — pick Latest or a
157|  newer pin. If the recommended knob sits above every published
158|  release, lower it to the newest release. Otherwise the runner is
159|  likely just busy: it converges at the next idle check, or press
160|  Update now (idle-only, never interrupts work). Restart does NOT
161|  clear this — Restart reboots the same version.
162|- **"restart queued" that never clears / restart loop.** The runner
163|  collects `requestRestart` on every heartbeat but never reboots:
164|  check the journal for the `Runner restarting` line. If the line is
165|  there but no reboot follows, the runner is not supervised by the
166|  wrapper (bare `node main.js` exits instead of rebooting — migrate to
167|  the wrapper, above) or the install root is unwritable (look for
168|  `sentinel not written`). A `restart-requested` file left behind by a
169|  crash causes at most one extra boot on the next clean exit — the
170|  wrapper consumes it, never loops. Old runners that predate the
171|  command show a disabled Restart with "too old" guidance instead —
172|  update them manually.
173|- **"below minimum" / 409 loop.** The runner is under
174|  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and dispatch refuses it. It
175|  self-updates immediately when idle (interval bypassed). If it
176|  spins, check the journal for `Runner update` lines and treat the
177|  reason like an "update failed" below.
178|- **"update failed".** The next heartbeat carries `updateStatus`
179|  (`state: failed`, `reason`, `at`) — the badge tooltip shows it.
180|  Map the reason prefix: signature/key failure (release not signed
181|  by the pinned key — never hand-edit
182|  `PINNED_RELEASE_PUBLIC_KEY` in `runner/updates/verify.js` for a
183|  cut release); sha mismatch (re-download on next check); no asset
184|  for this platform (release is missing this host's tarball);
185|  incompatible with this backend (no newer release admits this
186|  backend's API — expected while the backend lags the release
187|  line); update lock held (a previous updater is still running or
188|  crashed mid-apply — stale locks self-heal); opted out (see
189|  above). Any failure keeps the old version running; fix the cause
190|  and the next idle check retries.
191|- **"rolled back" in the doctor.** Three crashed boots flipped
192|  `current` back to `previous`. Do not retry blindly: read the
193|  journal for the crash, fix forward with a patch release, and run
194|  the rollback drill above if the release is bad fleet-wide.
195|
196|Backend-side checks: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and
197|`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` values, the fleet matrix row
198|for the runner (`runnerVersion`, `updateAvailable`, `belowMinimum`,
199|`updateStatus`), and whether a `requestUpdate` command is pending or
200|was acked within the last 24h (the auto-nudge cooldown).

Read text file `docs/KB Code Standards.md`.
1|# Values
2|
3|## User understandable over technical language
4|
5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible
6|
7|### Principles
8|
9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
12|- File structure should reflect the call stack
13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
14|- Include why things are done not just what is done
15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
18|- Every new export also carries a `MARK:` label in the same JSDoc block, sitting directly above the export (only whitespace between `*/` and `export`); `npm run check:jsdoc-example` (<1s) checks this before pushing — copy-paste shapes in docs/agent-docs/KB-Code-Standards.md §Documentation/Jsdoc
19|  
20|  
21|
22|## Functional over Object oreintated
23|
24|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).
25|
26|### Principles
27|
28|- Try and avoid using classes where possible
29|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
30|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
31|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
32|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
33|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
34|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility
35|
36|
37|## Co-location over abstraction
38|
39|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.
40|
41|### Principles
42|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
43|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
44|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
45|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
46|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
47|- Don’t fear repetition of code
48|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
49|- Use folders as a tool for organising
50|
51|## Tested over trusted 
52|
53|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 
54|
55|### Principles
56|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
57|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
58|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
59|- Tests must be consistent
60|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
61|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle
62|
63|
64|## Fast iteration over long planning
65|
66|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.
67|
68|### Principles
69|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
70|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
71|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
72|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
73|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
74|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
75|
76|
77|
78|# Inspirations
79|My principles here are inspired by:
80|
81|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
82|- Life isn’t binary (book)
83|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)
84|
85|
86|# Examples
87|
88|## Intent Driven descriptions
89|
90|### Bad Example
91|
92|```js
93|
94|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {
95|
96|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}
97|
98|    users.push(user)
99|  
100|}
101|
102|const list = []
103|
104|userFactory("Frank",32,list)
105|
106|
107|```
108|
109|## Good example
110|
111|```js
112|
113|/**
114|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
115|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
116|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
117|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
118|*/
119|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
120|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
121|  
122|  return ageNextYear
123|}
124|
125|const userObjectsList = []
126|
127|const usersName = "Frank"
128|const usersAge = 32
129|
130|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})
131|
132|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})
133|
134|
135|```

176|    stage-output commit matching the execution window. Present → Cause 2/4
177|    territory; absent → Cause 5 suspect. Record exact SHAs or exact absence.
178|2.2 Journal join (same host, same window): `Runner failed:` line text +
179|    restart-counter deltas — names hook/commit vs 413 vs 502/fetch-fail.
180|2.3 Fallback chain when a worktree is absent (already the case on server2-alpha
181|    for all four seeds): (a) check the sibling host; (b) check `origin` for the
182|    stage-output SHA (pushed = commit succeeded, Cause 2/4); (c) journal line
183|    alone; (d) if all absent, record an explicit evidence gap — never guess.
184|2.4 Verdict per interrupt: Cause-2/4 vs Cause-5-covered-by-`046a6391` vs
185|    Cause-5-NOT-covered. The third verdict is the ONLY trigger for new code:
186|    if and only if E5 finds commit-loop cases `046a6391` does not cover
187|    (a deterministic failure class outside `HOOK_REJECTED`/`COMMIT_FAILED`/
188|    `MERGE_CONFLICT` that still crash-loops on 0.2.x), file a NEW Cause-5
189|    code ticket with the journal line + worktree state + failing class.
190|
191|Gate: `E5-SWEEP.md` with one row per post-`finished` interrupt (evidence or
192|gap) + the ticket/no-ticket decision with reasoning.
193|
194|## Phase 3 — Convergence watch (the long pole; observe only)
195|
196|3.1 Poll `GET /runners` on a slow cadence (30–60 min) and snapshot each poll.
197|    Per runner record: running version + build facts, `updateAvailable` /
198|    `belowMinimum` / `updateStatus` badges, pending vs acked `requestUpdate`
199|    (nudge cooldown is 24 h), busy/idle, pinned-vs-Latest.
200|3.2 Declare a runner converged at the first poll showing a 0.2.x build whose
201|    release contains `046a6391`; record the converge timestamp per runner in
202|    `RUN-LOG.md`. Both converged → proceed to Phase 4 (q3 default).
203|3.3 If a runner stalls (badge never clears past 24–48 h): triage READ-ONLY per
204|    the runbook ("a runner says out of date") — `entrypoint: direct` vs
205|    wrapper, `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` opt-out, pinned version, pin
206|    older than running, recommended knob above every release, `updateStatus`
207|    failure reason — and record the blocking cause. Fixes (migrate, flip the
208|    switch, Update button) are PROD-ACTION: propose, do not perform.
209|3.4 NEVER to speed convergence: force-restart mid-assignment, Update-on-busy,
210|    reaping worktrees, re-running parked tasks. Any of these manufactures the
211|    interrupts being measured (q9 / PROD-ACTION ban).
212|
213|Gate: per-runner converge timestamps, or a stalled-runner triage note with a
214|named blocking cause. Under the q3-fallback (before-now/stop), Phase 3 becomes
215|a scheduled follow-up run instead of a same-run wait.
216|
217|## Phase 4 — AFTER recount + journal sweeps (after both converge)
218|
219|4.1 AFTER snapshot: raw `GET /runners` JSON + fleet script → `RECOUNT-AFTER.md`
220|    (§2 table + per-task rows), timestamped ≥ both converge times.
221|4.2 Split new interrupts at each runner's converge time; evaluate the S5 gates
222|    on post-converge interrupts only: bare → ~0; reasons name Causes 1/3/4
223|    (cap strings, setup-fault messages, transient 502/fetch-fail strings);
224|    deterministic commit failures arrive as FAILED completions carrying
225|    `gitFailure` payloads (`kind`/`phase`/`summary`) with NO interrupt row.
226|4.3 Journal sweeps (both hosts, post-converge window): E3 `Backend 413` lines
227|    (expect none-new after S2 lands; any 413 on 0.2.x must pair with a FAILED
228|    completion, never a crash loop), E4 502/`fetch failed` crash lines
229|    (expect crash-restarts to persist until S4 lands — reasons now name them),
230|    hook/commit lines (expect single `commit failed (...)` + FAILED, no
231|    restart storm).
232|4.4 Record confounds: backend build number at AFTER time, which of S1/S2/S4/S6
233|    have deployed, and any deploys that restarted the backend in-window
234|    (Cause-6 upkeep: any `interrupted by server restart` row re-opens it).
235|
236|Gate: `RECOUNT-AFTER.md` with the post-converge-gated verdict per S5 gate
237|(pass/fail + counts), plus the confound ledger.
238|
239|## Phase 5 — Baseline record + handoff (closes the task)
240|
241|5.1 Write `BASELINE.md`: the new S1–S4 reference — BEFORE/AFTER §2 tables,
242|    per-runner versions + converge timestamps, backend builds, window dates,
243|    E5 verdicts, open evidence gaps, and the exact re-run commands (Phase 0 kit).
244|5.2 Handoff notes: unblock prod CONFIRMATION of S3/S4/S2-runner-half (code work
245|    never waited); S1/S6 confirm against `BASELINE.md` + their own deploys.
246|    If 2.4 triggered, link the new Cause-5 ticket; otherwise state explicitly
247|    that no new Cause-5 code is needed.
248|5.3 Review-checklist pass (RESPONSE.md): no PROD command ran without permission;
249|    exhibit worktrees untouched; recount recorded before any victory claim.
250|
251|Gate: `BASELINE.md` present and self-contained — a stranger can re-run the
252|whole proof from the kit + this file alone.
253|
254|## Validation & assurance plan (how we know it worked)
255|
256|No unit tests by design (ops task — RESPONSE.md S5: "No new unit tests;
257|deliverable is the recount + version record"). Assurance instead comes from
258|executed procedures with saved evidence, each claim cross-checked two ways:
259|
260|| Claim | Primary evidence | Independent cross-check |
261||---|---|---|
262|| Runners on fix build | `GET /runners` version facts | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` + heartbeat build fields |
263|| Bare → ~0 | Fleet script `bare` count post-converge | Reason-vocabulary audit (1.3): every new interrupt carries a reason naming a cause |
264|| No commit crash-loops | FAILED + `gitFailure` completions, no interrupt row | Journal: single `commit failed` per incident, no restart storm |
265|| E5 classification | Worktree stage-output-commit presence | Journal `Runner failed:` line + origin SHA check |
266|| No server-restart orphans | `server_restart` count stays 0 | Backend build/`engine.updatedAt` divergence log (Cause-6 upkeep) |
267|
268|Per-phase gates above double as the test plan: a phase is done only when its
269|artifact file exists with the named content. Negative controls: (a) BEFORE
270|snapshot must show still-bare new interrupts (proves the premise that 0.1.0
271|emits no reasons); (b) any reasoned non-cap interrupt pre-converge, or any
272|bare interrupt post-converge, fails its gate and must be explained, not
273|averaged away. Docs assurance: every record file carries timestamps, raw
274|command output (or the raw JSON), and the exact re-run command.
275|
276|## Deliverables (all under `docs/tasks/683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c/`)
277|

279|  input) · `RUN-LOG.md` · `bin/fleet-recount.sh` · `bin/runners-snapshot.sh` ·

281|  `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md` · `RECOUNT-AFTER.md` · `E5-SWEEP.md` · `BASELINE.md`.
282|
283|## Risks & non-goals
284|
285|- Convergence may take >24 h per runner (daily nudge, idle-only). Mitigation:
286|  q3 default waits in-run; q3-fallback splits BEFORE/Phase 2 now, AFTER later.
287|- S1/S2/S4/S6 landing mid-window confounds attribution. Mitigation: confound

1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# fleet-recount.sh <label> [task-dir] — GUIDE-07 §5 fleet recount +
3|# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table, over one project, read-only against the
4|# backend API (approved: this task's SURVEY.md q2). Scope is pinned to project
5|# 0fd41821-... so results compare directly with the 2026-11-21 baseline.
6|#
7|# Outputs (under task-dir, default: current directory):
8|#   raw/<label>/<taskId>.json        raw GET /tasks/<id> payloads (evidence)
9|#   recount-<label>.jsonl            one aggregated row per task  (jq/per-task.jq)
10|#   recount-<label>-table.json       WIDE_NET §2 aggregate         (jq/aggregate.jq)
11|#   recount-<label>-e5worklist.json  post-finished interrupts      (jq/e5-worklist.jq, GUIDE-05 §4 scope)
12|#   recount-<label>-errors.jsonl     tasks that failed to fetch/parse (always created; empty when nothing failed)
13|#   recount-<label>-meta.json        run metadata (api, project, window, counts)
14|#   stdout                           the §2 table + E5 worklist, for the run log
15|#
16|# Crash safety: per-task rows accumulate in temp staging files and are moved
17|# into place only after the fetch loop finishes, so killing the script
18|# mid-run can never leave a truncated recount-<label>.jsonl beside a
19|# meta/table from an older run of the same label.
20|#
21|# Failure behaviour (deliberate, so a partial run is loud, never silent):
22|#   - the task list itself unreachable/invalid/empty -> exit 1, no outputs written
23|#   - one task fails to download or parse -> recorded in -errors.jsonl, the
24|#     loop continues, the table is still written, and the script exits 2 at
25|#     the end so the gap cannot be missed
26|#   - API base / project overridable via KAINBAIN_API_BASE / KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID
27|#     (the test suite drives this script against a local mock API)
28|set -euo pipefail
29|SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
30|# shellcheck source=lib.sh
31|source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"
32|
33|main() {
34|  require_commands curl jq date mktemp
35|  local label="${1:-}"
36|  [ -n "$label" ] || die "usage: fleet-recount.sh <before|after|...> [task-dir]"
37|  [ $# -le 2 ] || die "usage: fleet-recount.sh <before|after|...> [task-dir] — unexpected extra argument '$3'"
38|  validate_label "$label"
39|  local task_dir="${2:-$(pwd)}"
40|  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
41|  local project_id="${KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID:-0fd41821-d8a5-4e49-bc2e-28ce8c739a0a}"
42|  local raw_dir="$task_dir/raw/$label"
43|  mkdir -p "$raw_dir"
44|  local started; started="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
45|  log "fleet-recount label=$label api=$api_base project=$project_id task_dir=$task_dir started=$started"
46|
47|  # 1. task list — must be a non-empty array of well-formed ids, otherwise the
48|  #    API is down, the project id is wrong, or we got an error page.
49|  local list_tmp; list_tmp="$(mktemp)"
50|  if ! api_get_json "$api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id" "$list_tmp.list"; then
51|    rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
52|    die "cannot list tasks at $api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id — API down or wrong project; nothing written"
53|  fi
54|  local ids; ids="$(jq -r 'if type == "array" then (.[].id // empty) else empty end' "$list_tmp.list")"
55|  rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
56|  local n; n="$(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -c . || true)"
57|  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || die "GET /tasks returned zero tasks for project $project_id — refusing to write an empty baseline"
58|  if printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -qvE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'; then
59|    die "task list contains a malformed id — refusing to continue (got: $(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -vE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' | head -3 | tr '\n' ' '))"
60|  fi
61|  log "task list ok: $n tasks"
62|
63|  # 2. per-task fetch + aggregate row. One bad task never aborts the loop.
64|  # Rows accumulate in staging files first (see header: crash safety).
65|  local jsonl="$task_dir/recount-$label.jsonl" errors="$task_dir/recount-$label-errors.jsonl"
66|  local table="$task_dir/recount-$label-table.json" worklist="$task_dir/recount-$label-e5worklist.json"
67|  local jsonl_stage errors_stage row_tmp
68|  jsonl_stage="$(mktemp)"; errors_stage="$(mktemp)"; row_tmp="$(mktemp)"
69|  : > "$jsonl_stage"
70|  : > "$errors_stage"
71|  local ok=0 failed=0 t raw
72|  # ids are validated UUIDs above, so unquoted splitting here is safe.
73|  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
74|  for t in $ids; do
75|    raw="$raw_dir/$t.json"
76|    if api_get_json "$api_base/tasks/$t?projectId=$project_id" "$raw" \
77|       && jq -e 'type == "object" and ((.history // []) | type == "array")' "$raw" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
78|       && jq -c -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/per-task.jq" "$raw" > "$row_tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
79|      cat "$row_tmp" >> "$jsonl_stage"
80|      ok=$((ok + 1))
81|    else
82|      failed=$((failed + 1))
83|      rm -f "$raw"
84|      printf '{"task":"%s","error":"fetch or parse failed"}\n' "$t" >> "$errors_stage"
85|      log "WARN: task $t failed to fetch/parse — recorded in recount-$label-errors.jsonl, continuing"
86|    fi
87|  done
88|  rm -f "$row_tmp"
89|  write_atomic "$jsonl" "$jsonl_stage" || die "cannot publish $jsonl — previous file (if any) left untouched"
90|  write_atomic "$errors" "$errors_stage" || die "cannot publish $errors — $jsonl was published, rerun to regenerate"
91|  rm -f "$jsonl_stage" "$errors_stage"
92|  log "fetched $ok tasks, $failed failed"
93|
94|  # 3. aggregates (atomic writes), printed to stdout for the run log too.
95|  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/aggregate.jq" "$jsonl" > "$table.tmp.$$" && mv "$table.tmp.$$" "$table"
96|  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/e5-worklist.jq" "$jsonl" > "$worklist.tmp.$$" && mv "$worklist.tmp.$$" "$worklist"
97|  jq -n --arg label "$label" --arg api "$api_base" --arg project "$project_id" \
98|      --arg started "$started" --arg finished "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" \
99|      --argjson ok "$ok" --argjson failed "$failed" \
100|      '{label: $label, api: $api, project: $project, startedAt: $started, finishedAt: $finished, tasksFetched: $ok, tasksFailed: $failed}' \
101|    > "$task_dir/recount-$label-meta.json"
102|
103|  echo "## WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table — label=$label, project $project_id, $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
104|  jq . "$table"
105|  echo
106|  echo "## E5 worklist — post-finished interrupts (GUIDE-05 §4 scope), label=$label"
107|  jq . "$worklist"
108|  echo
109|  if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
110|    echo "## ERRORS — $failed task(s) failed, see recount-$label-errors.jsonl" >&2
111|    cat "$errors" >&2
112|    log "exiting 2: $failed of $n tasks failed"
113|    exit 2
114|  fi
115|  log "done: label=$label ok=$ok failed=$failed"
116|}
117|
118|if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
119|  main "$@"
120|fi

3|# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table, over one project, read-only against the
4|# backend API (approved: this task's SURVEY.md q2). Scope is pinned to project
5|# 0fd41821-... so results compare directly with the 2026-11-21 baseline.
6|#
7|# Outputs (under task-dir, default: current directory):
8|#   raw/<label>/<taskId>.json        raw GET /tasks/<id> payloads (evidence)
9|#   recount-<label>.jsonl            one aggregated row per task  (jq/per-task.jq)
10|#   recount-<label>-table.json       WIDE_NET §2 aggregate         (jq/aggregate.jq)
11|#   recount-<label>-e5worklist.json  post-finished interrupts      (jq/e5-worklist.jq, GUIDE-05 §4 scope)
12|#   recount-<label>-errors.jsonl     tasks that failed to fetch/parse (always created; empty when nothing failed)
13|#   recount-<label>-meta.json        run metadata (api, project, window, counts)
14|#   stdout                           the §2 table + E5 worklist, for the run log
15|#
16|# Crash safety: per-task rows accumulate in temp staging files and are moved
17|# into place only after the fetch loop finishes, so killing the script
18|# mid-run can never leave a truncated recount-<label>.jsonl beside a
19|# meta/table from an older run of the same label.
20|#
21|# Failure behaviour (deliberate, so a partial run is loud, never silent):
22|#   - the task list itself unreachable/invalid/empty -> exit 1, no outputs written
23|#   - one task fails to download or parse -> recorded in -errors.jsonl, the
24|#     loop continues, the table is still written, and the script exits 2 at
25|#     the end so the gap cannot be missed
26|#   - API base / project overridable via KAINBAIN_API_BASE / KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID
27|#     (the test suite drives this script against a local mock API)
28|set -euo pipefail
29|SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
30|# shellcheck source=lib.sh
31|source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"
32|
33|main() {
34|  require_commands curl jq date mktemp
35|  local label="${1:-}"
36|  [ -n "$label" ] || die "usage: fleet-recount.sh <before|after|...> [task-dir]"
37|  [ $# -le 2 ] || die "usage: fleet-recount.sh <before|after|...> [task-dir] — unexpected extra argument '$3'"
38|  validate_label "$label"
39|  local task_dir="${2:-$(pwd)}"
40|  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
41|  local project_id="${KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID:-0fd41821-d8a5-4e49-bc2e-28ce8c739a0a}"
42|  local raw_dir="$task_dir/raw/$label"
43|  mkdir -p "$raw_dir"
44|  local started; started="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
45|  log "fleet-recount label=$label api=$api_base project=$project_id task_dir=$task_dir started=$started"
46|
47|  # 1. task list — must be a non-empty array of well-formed ids, otherwise the
48|  #    API is down, the project id is wrong, or we got an error page.
49|  local list_tmp; list_tmp="$(mktemp)"
50|  if ! api_get_json "$api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id" "$list_tmp.list"; then
51|    rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
52|    die "cannot list tasks at $api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id — API down or wrong project; nothing written"
53|  fi
54|  local ids; ids="$(jq -r 'if type == "array" then (.[].id // empty) else empty end' "$list_tmp.list")"
55|  rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
56|  local n; n="$(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -c . || true)"
57|  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || die "GET /tasks returned zero tasks for project $project_id — refusing to write an empty baseline"
58|  if printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -qvE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'; then
59|    die "task list contains a malformed id — refusing to continue (got: $(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -vE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' | head -3 | tr '\n' ' '))"
60|  fi
61|  log "task list ok: $n tasks"
62|
63|  # 2. per-task fetch + aggregate row. One bad task never aborts the loop.
64|  # Rows accumulate in staging files first (see header: crash safety).
65|  local jsonl="$task_dir/recount-$label.jsonl" errors="$task_dir/recount-$label-errors.jsonl"
66|  local table="$task_dir/recount-$label-table.json" worklist="$task_dir/recount-$label-e5worklist.json"
67|  local jsonl_stage errors_stage row_tmp
68|  jsonl_stage="$(mktemp)"; errors_stage="$(mktemp)"; row_tmp="$(mktemp)"
69|  : > "$jsonl_stage"
70|  : > "$errors_stage"
71|  local ok=0 failed=0 t raw
72|  # ids are validated UUIDs above, so unquoted splitting here is safe.
73|  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
74|  for t in $ids; do
75|    raw="$raw_dir/$t.json"
76|    if api_get_json "$api_base/tasks/$t?projectId=$project_id" "$raw" \
77|       && jq -e 'type == "object" and ((.history // []) | type == "array")' "$raw" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
78|       && jq -c -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/per-task.jq" "$raw" > "$row_tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
79|      cat "$row_tmp" >> "$jsonl_stage"
80|      ok=$((ok + 1))
81|    else
82|      failed=$((failed + 1))
83|      rm -f "$raw"
84|      printf '{"task":"%s","error":"fetch or parse failed"}\n' "$t" >> "$errors_stage"
85|      log "WARN: task $t failed to fetch/parse — recorded in recount-$label-errors.jsonl, continuing"
86|    fi
87|  done
88|  rm -f "$row_tmp"
89|  write_atomic "$jsonl" "$jsonl_stage" || die "cannot publish $jsonl — previous file (if any) left untouched"
90|  write_atomic "$errors" "$errors_stage" || die "cannot publish $errors — $jsonl was published, rerun to regenerate"
91|  rm -f "$jsonl_stage" "$errors_stage"
92|  log "fetched $ok tasks, $failed failed"
93|
94|  # 3. aggregates (atomic writes), printed to stdout for the run log too.
95|  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/aggregate.jq" "$jsonl" > "$table.tmp.$$" && mv "$table.tmp.$$" "$table"
96|  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/e5-worklist.jq" "$jsonl" > "$worklist.tmp.$$" && mv "$worklist.tmp.$$" "$worklist"
97|  jq -n --arg label "$label" --arg api "$api_base" --arg project "$project_id" \
98|      --arg started "$started" --arg finished "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" \
99|      --argjson ok "$ok" --argjson failed "$failed" \
100|      '{label: $label, api: $api, project: $project, startedAt: $started, finishedAt: $finished, tasksFetched: $ok, tasksFailed: $failed}' \
101|    > "$task_dir/recount-$label-meta.json"
102|
103|  echo "## WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table — label=$label, project $project_id, $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
104|  jq . "$table"
105|  echo
106|  echo "## E5 worklist — post-finished interrupts (GUIDE-05 §4 scope), label=$label"
107|  jq . "$worklist"
108|  echo
109|  if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
110|    echo "## ERRORS — $failed task(s) failed, see recount-$label-errors.jsonl" >&2
111|    cat "$errors" >&2
112|    log "exiting 2: $failed of $n tasks failed"
113|    exit 2
114|  fi
115|  log "done: label=$label ok=$ok failed=$failed"
116|}
117|
118|if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
119|  main "$@"
120|fi
